recommendation: Give generously to support the community of monks and the world, as the Chief Almsgiver did.
evidence_quote: Anathapindika was one of the eighty chief disciples who bore the title of Chief Almsgiver.
rationale: The gift is blessed to promote righteousness and to be a lasting blessing to mankind and especially to the giver.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Give lifelong support such as robes, food, and medicine to the monks and nuns, including the sick and their caretakers.
evidence_quote: I desire, Lord, through all my life to bestow robes for the rainy season on the Sangha
rationale: none given

recommendation: Cultivate yourself in reverent carefulness, so as to give rest to others and to all the people.
evidence_quote: He cultivates himself so as to give rest to all the people.
rationale: Even the great sage rulers were still concerned about giving rest to all the people.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Be humble as a junior, do something worthy of being remembered in manhood, and do not live on to old age as a pest.
evidence_quote: In youth not humble as befits a junior; in manhood, doing nothing worthy of being handed down; and living on to old age:-- this is to be a pest.
rationale: The Master scolded a man who failed in these ways, calling him a pest.
scope: all stages of life: youth, manhood, old age
argued_against: being disrespectful in youth, achieving nothing in manhood, and lingering uselessly in old age

recommendation: Rulers should love to observe the rules of propriety.
evidence_quote: When rulers love to observe the rules of propriety, the people respond readily to the calls on them for service.
rationale: When rulers love propriety, the people respond readily to calls for service.

recommendation: Endure want with composure and do not give way to unbridled license when in poverty.
evidence_quote: The superior man may indeed have to endure want, but the mean man, when he is in want, gives way to unbridled license.
rationale: none given
scope: the superior man in times of want
argued_against: the mean man who gives way to unbridled license in want

recommendation: Seek a single all-pervading principle rather than only memorizing many things.
evidence_quote: No,' was the answer; 'I seek a unity all-pervading.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: learning many things and merely keeping them in memory

recommendation: Let your words be sincere and truthful and your actions honorable and careful, and keep these constantly before you.
evidence_quote: Let his words be sincere and truthful, and his actions honourable and careful
rationale: Such conduct works everywhere, even among rude tribes; without it a person will not be appreciated even in his own neighborhood.
argued_against: insincere words and dishonorable, careless actions

recommendation: Speak to those who can be spoken with, and do not waste words on those who cannot.
evidence_quote: The wise err neither in regard to their man nor to their words.
rationale: Not speaking to a receptive man wrongs the man; speaking to an unreceptive man wastes words.
conditions: depends on whether the person can be spoken with
argued_against: speaking to the wrong people or staying silent with the right ones

recommendation: Be ready to sacrifice your life rather than injure your virtue.
evidence_quote: They will even sacrifice their lives to preserve their virtue complete.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: the determined scholar and the man of virtue
argued_against: living at the expense of virtue

recommendation: In any state, take service with the most worthy officers and make friends of the most virtuous scholars.
evidence_quote: When you are living in any state, take service with the most worthy among its great officers, and make friends of the most virtuous among its scholars.
rationale: A mechanic who wishes to do his work well must first sharpen his tools; good associates are the tools for practicing virtue.
scope: anyone living in a state who wishes to practice virtue

recommendation: Banish licentious songs and keep far from specious talkers.
evidence_quote: Banish the songs of Chang, and keep far from specious talkers.
rationale: The songs are licentious and specious talkers are dangerous.

recommendation: Think about what is distant.
evidence_quote: If a man take no thought about what is distant, he will find sorrow near at hand.
rationale: A man who does not think of what is distant will find sorrow near at hand.

recommendation: Love virtue as much as you love beauty.
evidence_quote: I have not seen one who loves virtue as he loves beauty.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not hide worthy people; promote talented and virtuous men to office when you know them.
evidence_quote: He knew the virtue and the talents of Hui of Liu-hsia, and yet did not procure that he should stand with him in court.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: officials who know of worthy men
argued_against: an official who holds his post like one who stole it and does not recommend a worthy man

recommendation: Require much from yourself and little from others.
evidence_quote: He who requires much from himself and little from others, will keep himself from being the object of resentment.
rationale: This keeps you from being the object of resentment.

recommendation: Habitually ask yourself what you should think about a matter.
evidence_quote: What shall I think of this? What shall I think of this?
rationale: The Master can do nothing with a man who does not ask this.

recommendation: Do not spend whole days in talk that never turns to righteousness or in relying on small shrewdness.
evidence_quote: for a whole day, without their conversation turning on righteousness
rationale: Such a group is in a hard case.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: conversation that avoids righteousness and fondness for small shrewdness

recommendation: Treat righteousness as essential in everything: practice it according to propriety, with humility, and complete it with sincerity.
evidence_quote: The superior man in everything considers righteousness to be essential.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Be distressed by your own lack of ability, not by other people not knowing you.
evidence_quote: The superior man is distressed by his want of ability. He is not distressed by men's not knowing him.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Seek what you need in yourself, not in others.
evidence_quote: What the superior man seeks, is in himself. What the mean man seeks, is in others.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: the mean man who looks to others

recommendation: Be dignified but do not wrangle; be sociable but do not join a faction.
evidence_quote: The superior man is dignified, but does not wrangle. He is sociable, but not a partizan.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not promote a man just because of his words, and do not dismiss good words because of the man.
evidence_quote: The superior man does not promote a man simply on account of his words, nor does he put aside good words because of the man.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: judging by words alone or by the speaker alone

recommendation: Practice reciprocity: do not do to others what you do not want done to yourself.
evidence_quote: What you do not want done to yourself, do not do to others.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: all people; a rule of practice for all one's life

recommendation: Do not blame or praise others beyond what is proper; base any praise on examination of the person.
evidence_quote: whose evil do I blame, whose goodness do I praise, beyond what is proper?
rationale: Any praise given must have ground in an examination of the individual.

recommendation: Be forbearing in small matters, and avoid specious words that confuse virtue.
evidence_quote: Specious words confound virtue. Want of forbearance in small matters confounds great plans.
rationale: Specious words confound virtue and lack of forbearance in small things ruins great plans.
argued_against: specious words and impatience over small matters

recommendation: When the crowd hates or likes a man, examine the case yourself.
evidence_quote: When the multitude hate a man, it is necessary to examine into the case. When the multitude like a man, it is necessary to examine into the case.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Reform your faults; do not keep them.
evidence_quote: To have faults and not to reform them,-- this, indeed, should be pronounced having faults.
rationale: A fault that is not reformed is what truly counts as a fault.

recommendation: Learn even if you are dull and stupid; those who stay dull and do not learn are the lowest of people.
evidence_quote: As to those who are dull and stupid and yet do not learn;-- they are the lowest of the people.
rationale: Those who are dull but still compass learning rank above those who do not learn.
argued_against: dull people who do not learn

recommendation: Give careful thought to nine things: seeing clearly, hearing distinctly, a benign countenance, respectful demeanor, sincere speech, reverently careful work, asking others when in doubt.
evidence_quote: The superior man has nine things which are subjects with him of thoughtful consideration.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: When angry, think of the difficulties your anger may bring; when you see gain, think of righteousness.
evidence_quote: When he is angry, he thinks of the difficulties (his anger may involve him in). When he sees gain to be got, he thinks of righteousness.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: acting on anger or greed without thought

recommendation: Pursue good as if you could never reach it, and shrink from evil as from boiling water.
evidence_quote: Contemplating good, and pursuing it, as if they could not reach it; contemplating evil, and shrinking from it, as they would from thrusting the hand into boiling water
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Live in retirement to study your aims and practice righteousness to carry out your principles.
evidence_quote: Living in retirement to study their aims, and practising righteousness to carry out their principles
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Be remembered for virtue, not for wealth: lasting praise goes to virtue, not riches.
evidence_quote: the people did not praise him for a single virtue. Po-i and Shu-ch'i died of hunger at the foot of the Shau-yang mountain, and the people, down to the present time, praise them.
rationale: A duke with a thousand teams of horses was not praised at death, while two men who starved are still praised.

recommendation: Learn the Odes and the rules of Propriety.
evidence_quote: If you do not learn the Odes, you will not be fit to converse with.
rationale: Without the Odes you are unfit for conversation; without the rules of Propriety your character cannot be established.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: neglecting study of the Odes and propriety

recommendation: Keep a distant reserve toward your son.
evidence_quote: the superior man maintains a distant reserve towards his son.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: the superior man as a father

recommendation: Practice five things everywhere: gravity, generosity of soul, sincerity, earnestness, and kindness.
evidence_quote: Gravity, generosity of soul, sincerity, earnestness, and kindness.
rationale: Gravity prevents disrespect, generosity wins all, sincerity brings trust, earnestness accomplishes much, and kindness lets you employ others.

recommendation: Pair every virtue with a love of learning; benevolence, knowing, sincerity, straightforwardness, boldness, and firmness without learning turn into faults.
evidence_quote: There is the love of being benevolent without the love of learning;-- the beclouding here leads to a foolish simplicity.
rationale: Each virtue without learning leads to a fault: foolish simplicity, dissipation of mind, injurious disregard of consequences, rudeness, insubordination, or extravagant conduct.
scope: all who love these six virtues
argued_against: loving a virtue without the love of learning

recommendation: Study the Book of Poetry, and give yourself to the Chau-nan and the Shao-nan.
evidence_quote: My children, why do you not study the Book of Poetry?
rationale: The Odes stimulate the mind, aid self-contemplation, teach sociability, regulate resentment, teach duty to father and prince, and teach names of birds, beasts, and plants.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: not studying the Odes, like facing a wall

recommendation: Do not put on an appearance of stern firmness while being weak inside.
evidence_quote: He who puts on an appearance of stern firmness, while inwardly he is weak, is like one of the small, mean people
rationale: Such a person is like a thief who breaks through or climbs over a wall.
argued_against: false outward firmness with inner weakness

recommendation: Do not be a merely good, careful villager who pleases everyone; this robs virtue.
evidence_quote: Your good, careful people of the villages are the thieves of virtue.
rationale: Such people are called thieves of virtue.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not repeat on the road what you have just heard.
evidence_quote: To tell, as we go along, what we have heard on the way, is to cast away our virtue.
rationale: Spreading what you hear casts away your virtue.

recommendation: Do not nurse sorrow when you lose loved ones, since parting is certain for all beings.
evidence_quote: what wise man would cherish sorrow, when he loses his kindred, even though he loves them ?
rationale: Parting is fixed in time for all beings, like travellers who joined company on a road; sorrow is caused by ignorance, not by kin.
argued_against: cherishing sorrow over loss of kin

recommendation: Understand that sorrow comes only from ignorance, not from a son or kindred.
evidence_quote: neither a son nor kindred is the cause of sorrow,—this sorrow is caused only by ignorance.
rationale: Having seen the multiform in its developments, one sees sorrow comes from ignorance.

recommendation: Do not accept royal power; the wise should not enter royalty, the home of illusion.
evidence_quote: How can it be right for the wise to enter royalty, the home of illusion
rationale: Royalty brings anxiety, passion, weariness, and violation of right; accepting it from greed is like a sick man taking unwholesome food.
argued_against: taking a kingdom out of greed

recommendation: Do not rely on another's belief or an uncertain tradition; find out the truth for yourself.
evidence_quote: what wise man would go by another’s belief ?
rationale: Mankind following belief is like the blind directed in darkness by the blind; the sacred tradition is uncertain.
argued_against: accepting theories on the unknown or others' belief

recommendation: Even when unsure of the truth, set your mind on the good; toil in vain is worth choosing for a good soul.
evidence_quote: if good and evil are doubted, let one’s mind be set on the good
rationale: Even a toil in vain is to be chosen by one whose soul is good.
scope: when good and evil are in doubt
conditions: applies when the truth cannot be discerned

recommendation: Accept as right only what the trustworthy, those free of faults, have said.
evidence_quote: that only is right which has been uttered by the trustworthy
rationale: Trustworthiness means absence of faults, and one without faults will not utter an untruth.

recommendation: Do not cite as authorities those who have broken their vows when determining duty.
evidence_quote: how canst thou quote as authorities those who have broken their vows ?
rationale: Such examples have no authority in determining duty.

recommendation: Hold firm to your resolve for liberation and never return to worldly life with the senses alert only for outer objects.
evidence_quote: I would enter the blazing fire, but not my house with my purpose unfulfilled.
rationale: none given
scope: one who has set out to seek liberation
argued_against: returning home as a man of the world

recommendation: Do not leave your father in his old age to sorrow; duty comes before an unseen result.
evidence_quote: it could not be thy duty, loving duty as thou dost, to leave thy father in his old age to sorrow.
rationale: Leaving for an unseen result disregards a visible end; the resolve is unfit at the present time.
scope: the prince, as a loving son
argued_against: giving up a visible end for an unseen result

recommendation: Since the afterlife is doubtful, enjoy the good fortune that comes into your hand.
evidence_quote: since then the matter is all in doubt, it is right to enjoy the good fortune which comes into thy hand.
rationale: If there is activity hereafter we enjoy it; if not, liberation comes without effort.
conditions: applies since opinions on rebirth are in doubt
argued_against: giving up visible good for an unseen result

recommendation: Follow the prescribed rule, including debts to ancestors, saints, and gods, if you love liberation.
evidence_quote: if thou hast a love for liberation, follow rightly the prescribed rule
rationale: A man is born with 3 debts, to ancestors by offspring, to saints by lore, to gods by sacrifice; the wise promise liberation to him who uses effort.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Forsake vile connections and live at ease.
evidence_quote: forsake them and live at ease
rationale: Those who form vile connections will certainly suffer for them.

recommendation: Do not give yourself to sensual pleasures.
evidence_quote: He who is devoted to sesnual pleasures shah never know the joys of the -next world.
rationale: The sensualist will never know the joys of the next world.

recommendation: Beware of courtesans and lovely women; they strip you of your money.
evidence_quote: At the sight of her charms you are melted with love, a.nd the courtezan strips you of every farthing.
rationale: A courtesan takes every farthing; lovely women are darts in Cupid's hand.
argued_against: being melted by a courtesan's charms

recommendation: Do not rely on pilgrimage or ritual bathing; if your heart is right, God is here as in Benares.
evidence_quote: yet is not same God here as there ? If thy heart be right he is there and here also.
rationale: God is the same everywhere; a right heart finds him anywhere.
argued_against: pilgrimage to holy places as a means to God

recommendation: Do not bathe in holy waters or worship while your heart is full of hypocrisy.
evidence_quote: Why attempt to worship the deity while your bellies are full of foul hypocrisy ?
rationale: Outward rites are pointless while the heart is full of hypocrisy.

recommendation: Do not wander to holy places; it is mere drudgery that wastes money and brings no benefit.
evidence_quote: Fools roam to holy places imagining that the deity is not to be found where they dwell
rationale: Pilgrims only exercise their limbs and squander money; they return ruined and without benefit.
argued_against: fools who roam to holy places

recommendation: Worship and know Him who dwells in your heart, not through reading or monkish life.
evidence_quote: worship Him, and know Him who dwells in your heart
rationale: Reading and monkish life bear no fruit.

recommendation: Do not over-study or become a disputer; excessive study does not bring divine knowledge.
evidence_quote: Excessive study leads only to disputatious talking
rationale: It leads only to disputation, and the person is entangled like a silkworm in its shell.

recommendation: Do not scorn this excellent knowledge or learn only abstruse sciences.
evidence_quote: Those who look upon this excellent knowledge with scorn, and learn only abstruse sciences, shall not attain to it
rationale: Scorners never know the society of the good and wise and end in misery.
argued_against: scorning this knowledge and learning only abstruse sciences

recommendation: Hold to this knowledge, give up all other cares, and restrain your mind from wandering.
evidence_quote: And he who holds this superexcellent, who gives up all other caresj who lets not his mind wander, but restrains it, he shall stand fast without fail
rationale: He shall stand fast without fail, all his wishes shall be accomplished, and his soul shall be full of glory.
argued_against: a wandering mind and divided cares

recommendation: Do not base your religion on belief in Brahma; it is unreal and such a religion is useless.
evidence_quote: So Brahma is not real and any religion based upon it is useless.
rationale: No one has ever seen Brahma, and talk of union with him is like blind men leading blind men and produces no fruitful result.
argued_against: religion based on Brahma and Brahmin talk of union with him

recommendation: Do not base your religion on belief in a soul; it is speculation and not worth having.
evidence_quote: A religion based on soul is therefore not worth having.
rationale: The soul is unseen and unknown, belief in it is unprofitable, it leads to superstition, and it gives priests complete control over man.

recommendation: Accept something as real only if it shows itself in visible results.
evidence_quote: An invisible thing must show itself in some other form that is visible. Then alone it can be called real.
rationale: Electricity is accepted because of its results such as light; a legal fiction is accepted because it gives a fruitful and just result.
argued_against: accepting unseen things that give no results

recommendation: Do not spend time arguing about whether the soul or God exists; such discussion is unprofitable.
evidence_quote: the discussion of the existence of the soul is as unprofitable as the discussion of the existence of God.
rationale: Such discussion is unprofitable.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: speculation about the soul and God

recommendation: Cultivate right view (Samma Ditthi) and avoid beliefs that work against it.
evidence_quote: the belief in the existence of the soul is as much against the cultivation of Samma Ditthi as the belief in the existence of God.
rationale: Belief in soul or God is against the cultivation of right view and is a source of superstition.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: belief in the existence of a soul or God

recommendation: Serve your lord with spontaneous devotion, without regard to self-interest, fraud, or your own ends in this life or the next.
evidence_quote: to serve my lord with spontaneous devotion, without any regard to self-interest, fraud
rationale: Submission is the most imperative duty.

recommendation: Obey the order of a father, mother, guru, or master.
evidence_quote: and let me obey it
rationale: Such orders support righteousness, and obedience is the one means for every success: glory, salvation, and power.
scope: all people toward parents, guru, and master

recommendation: Endure a grievous burden for the good of your people and family.
evidence_quote: endure the grievous burden and make your people and family happy
rationale: In an emergency a brother is used as a shield, as the hand parries a sword stroke; the times are out of joint.

recommendation: Love Rama; anyone who invokes Bharat and still finds loving Rama hard is a monster.
evidence_quote: is a monster without a parallel
rationale: Hearing of such perfect devotion should make one love Rama and his feet.
scope: all who hear of Bharat's nature

recommendation: Do not be deceitful, crafty, or glad of another's loss like Indra.
evidence_quote: he loves another's loss and his own gain
rationale: Indra's ways are like a crow's, crafty and disreputable; Rama says he is like a dog.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: deceit and delighting in another's loss

recommendation: Retire into your own little territory, do not distract or strain yourself, and look at things as a human being, a citizen, and a mortal.
evidence_quote: Remember to retire into this little territory of thy own, and above all do not distract or strain thyself
rationale: none given

recommendation: Remember that external things do not touch the soul; disturbances come only from your own opinion.
evidence_quote: things do not touch the soul, for they are external and remain immovable; but our perturbations come only from the opinion which is within
rationale: Things are external and immovable, so disturbances arise only from inner opinion.

recommendation: Keep in mind that everything you see changes and will soon be gone, as you have already witnessed.
evidence_quote: constantly bear in mind how many of these changes thou hast already witnessed
rationale: All these things change immediately and will no longer be; the universe is transformation.

recommendation: Regard yourself as a member of a common political community with all people, governed by common reason.
evidence_quote: we are fellow-citizens; if this is so, we are members of some political community
rationale: Reason is common to all, so the law that commands what to do is common, and the world is a state.

recommendation: Do not be ashamed of death; it is a mystery of nature like birth.
evidence_quote: altogether not a thing of which any man should be ashamed
rationale: Death is composition and decomposition of the same elements, not contrary to the nature of a reasonable animal.

recommendation: Remember that soon both you and the one who wrongs you will be dead, and your names forgotten.
evidence_quote: within a very short time both thou and he will be dead; and soon not even your names will be left behind
rationale: It is natural and necessary that such persons act so, and both will be dead soon.
argued_against: resentment of those who act badly

recommendation: Drop your opinion that you have been harmed; without the complaint the harm is gone.
evidence_quote: Take away thy opinion, and then there is taken away the complaint, "I have been harmed."
rationale: What does not make a man worse does not make his life worse or harm him.
argued_against: the complaint of having been harmed

recommendation: Consider that everything that happens happens justly, and whatever you do, do it in keeping with being good.
evidence_quote: Consider that everything which happens, happens justly
rationale: Careful observation shows events are just, as if assigned by one who gives each thing its value.

recommendation: Do not hold the opinion of things that a wrongdoer holds or wants you to hold; see them as they are in truth.
evidence_quote: look at them as they are in truth
rationale: none given
argued_against: adopting the opinion of one who wrongs you

recommendation: Keep 2 rules ready: do only what reason suggests for people's use, and change your opinion if corrected, but only through persuasion.
evidence_quote: A man should always have these two rules in readiness
rationale: none given
conditions: Change of opinion must come from persuasion by justice or common advantage, not from pleasure or reputation
argued_against: changing opinion for pleasure or reputation

recommendation: Use your reason.
evidence_quote: Hast thou reason? I have.--Why then dost not thou use it?
rationale: If reason does its own work, nothing else is needed.

recommendation: Return to your principles and the worship of reason.
evidence_quote: if thou wilt return to thy principles and the worship of reason
rationale: Within 10 days you will seem a god to those who now see you as a beast and an ape.

recommendation: Do not act as if you would live 10,000 years; be good while it is in your power.
evidence_quote: Do not act as if thou wert going to live ten thousand years.
rationale: Death hangs over you.
conditions: while you live and it is in your power
argued_against: wasting time as though life were endless

recommendation: Do not look at what your neighbor says, does, or thinks; look only to making your own actions just and pure.
evidence_quote: How much trouble he avoids who does not look to see what his neighbor says or does or thinks
rationale: This avoids much trouble.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: looking round at the depraved morals of others

recommendation: Do not desire posthumous fame or praise; those who remember you will die too.
evidence_quote: He who has a vehement desire for posthumous fame does not consider that every one of those who remember him will himself also die very soon
rationale: Remembrance fades; praise is useful only for a certain utility; a beautiful thing is neither worse nor better for being praised.
argued_against: a vehement desire for posthumous fame and admiration of praise

recommendation: Do not be whirled about; in every movement respect justice and keep your faculty of understanding.
evidence_quote: Do not be whirled about, but in every movement have respect to justice
rationale: none given

recommendation: Accept everything that nature brings in its seasons as fruit for you.
evidence_quote: Everything is fruit to me which thy seasons bring, O Nature
rationale: All things come from, are in, and return to nature.

recommendation: Do only what is necessary and what your social nature requires, and remove unnecessary acts and thoughts.
evidence_quote: Do what is necessary, and whatever the reason of the animal which is naturally social requires
rationale: This brings the tranquillity of doing well and of doing few things, plus more leisure and less uneasiness, since most of what we say and do is unnecessary.

recommendation: Cultivate a good manner; it wins affection and makes everything easier.
evidence_quote: a good manner steals into the affections
rationale: A bad manner spoils even reason and justice; a good one sweetens truth, brings joy, and helps out of difficulty.

recommendation: Keep wise men around you as ministering spirits and use them.
evidence_quote: 'Tis a rare greatness to make use of the wise
rationale: They free you from fear of ignorance, solve difficulties, and let you speak with the authority of many sages.

recommendation: If you cannot have sages in your service, have them as friends.
evidence_quote: he that cannot have sages in service should have them for his friends
rationale: none given
conditions: applies to someone who cannot have sages as servants

recommendation: Join knowledge with good intentions.
evidence_quote: Knowledge and Good Intentions together ensure continuance of success.
rationale: Together they ensure lasting success; a clever mind with a wicked will ruins things more subtly, and knowledge without sense is double folly.
argued_against: a wicked will helped by knowledge

recommendation: Vary your mode of action; do not always act the same way or on first impulse.
evidence_quote: not always the same way, so as to distract attention
rationale: Others recognize uniformity and anticipate it, frustrating your designs; a twisting bird is harder to hit.
conditions: especially important if there is a rival or enemy

recommendation: Combine application with ability; work hard, since effort is the price of reputation.
evidence_quote: Work is the price which is paid for reputation.
rationale: No eminence is reached without both; mediocrity with application beats superiority without it; what costs little is little worth.

recommendation: Do not be content with humble mediocrity when you could shine among the highest.
evidence_quote: not so to be content with humble mediocrity when you could shine among the highest
rationale: none given
conditions: applies to those able to shine at the highest level

recommendation: Do not arouse exaggerated expectations when you begin; let reality exceed what was hoped.
evidence_quote: Arouse no Exaggerated Expectations on entering.
rationale: The real never equals the imagined; disappointed people are readier to disillusion than admire. A few creditable attempts suffice.
conditions: the rule does not apply to the wicked, who gain from exaggeration

recommendation: Help your luck with care, and press forward boldly instead of waiting at fortune's gate.
evidence_quote: it can be assisted by care
rationale: There are rules of luck; those who press forward win her favor; true luck or ill-luck is only wisdom or its opposite.
argued_against: merely waiting confidently for fortune to open the gate

recommendation: Arm yourself with tasteful, practical knowledge and a store of wise sayings and noble deeds, used on fitting occasions.
evidence_quote: Wise men arm themselves with tasteful and elegant erudition
rationale: A jest often teaches more than serious teaching; pat knowledge helps more than the liberal arts.

recommendation: Be spotless; remove your weak points and turn unavoidable flaws into ornament.
evidence_quote: Be Spotless: the indispensable condition of perfection.
rationale: A single slight defect can hide many qualities, as a cloud hides the sun, and ill-will notices it; many pamper curable faults.
scope: everyone, since few live without a weak point
argued_against: pampering weak points that could easily be cured

recommendation: Keep your imagination under control, sometimes correcting and sometimes assisting it.
evidence_quote: Keep the Imagination under Control
rationale: It governs happiness, makes us content or discontent, and can tyrannize through folly unless prudent self-control subdues it.
argued_against: letting imagination tyrannize, whipping fools with penalties or luring with delusion

recommendation: Know how to take a hint; be slow to believe favorable news and quick to believe unfavorable.
evidence_quote: Know how to take a Hint.
rationale: Fine talk is no longer enough; vital truths can only be half spoken, so attention is needed to grasp the whole.

recommendation: Find each man's ruling passion and appeal to it to move his will.
evidence_quote: Find out each Man's Thumbscrew.
rationale: Every volition has a motive; knowing a man's main spring is the key to his will, and men are idolaters of fame, interest, or pleasure.

recommendation: Prize intensity more than extent; value quality over quantity.
evidence_quote: Prize Intensity more than Extent.
rationale: Excellence lies in quality; the best is few and rare, much lowers value, extent alone never rises above mediocrity, and intensity gives eminence.
argued_against: judging by bulk, and universal geniuses at home nowhere

recommendation: Aim to be right about truth and Deliverance, humble, free of sloth, torpor and doubt, and the opposite of wrath, envy, avarice, deceit and arrogance, even if others are not.
evidence_quote: though others may be puffed up, you will be humble-minded
rationale: none given
scope: not stated; applies whatever others do
argued_against: others who are in error, slothful, puffed up, doubtful, wrathful, envious, deceitful

recommendation: Seek the Lord's doctrine, not the world's goods.
evidence_quote: be ye partakers not of the world's goods but of my doctrine
rationale: The Lord's compassion for them.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Shed greed, resentment, anger, malevolence, envy, jealousy, avarice, hypocrisy, arrogance, inflation, and indolence by following the Middle Way, the Noble Eight-fold Path.
evidence_quote: greed is vile, and vile is resentment
rationale: These vices are vile; the Eight-fold Path gives insight, peace, enlightenment and Nibbana.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: greed, resentment, anger, malevolence, envy, jealousy, niggardliness, hypocrisy, deceit, arrogance, inflation, indolence

recommendation: Develop right outlook, seeing life as a process of causal law; know what is right rather than merely being right.
evidence_quote: To be right one must know what is right.
rationale: Right thinking is the key to the higher life; lack of understanding is the root of all evil; perverted views lead all action to pain.
scope: all followers of the Eightfold path
argued_against: perverted views, aims, speech, action, and ignorance

recommendation: Do not speculate about whether the Tathagata exists beyond death; such questions do not help the holy life.
evidence_quote: a question not concerned with profit to humanity or with the first principles of holy life
rationale: Such questions do not lead to perfect wisdom or Nibbana, so they were left undeclared.

recommendation: Do not rely on invoking and praying to gods for union with Brahma; practice the qualities that make a true Brahmin.
evidence_quote: omitting the practice of those qualities which really make a man a Brahmin
rationale: Praying and hoping no more bring one to Brahma than invoking the far bank brings it across the river.
scope: Brahmins and others who pray in this way
argued_against: Brahmins who call on gods while neglecting true virtue

recommendation: Follow truth always and in all things; hate a lie utterly.
evidence_quote: Truth ... was his leader, whom he followed always and in all things
rationale: A follower of truth cannot be suspected of evil; with truth as captain, justice, health of mind, and temperance follow.
scope: the true philosopher or lover of knowledge
argued_against: imposture and love of a lie

recommendation: Keep striving toward true being, and do not rest until you have grasped the real nature of each essence.
evidence_quote: the true lover of knowledge is always striving after being
rationale: Only by that striving does one gain mind and truth, live and grow truly.
argued_against: resting in the multiplicity of individual appearances

recommendation: Whoever wants to be governed should go to one able to govern; the good ruler should not beg subjects to be ruled by him.
evidence_quote: he who wants to be governed, to him who is able to govern
rationale: As a sick man goes to the physician, rich or poor, and the pilot does not beg the sailors; this is the order of nature.
argued_against: the saying that the wise go to the doors of the rich; present rulers like mutinous sailors

recommendation: Blame the uselessness of philosophers on those who will not use them, not on the philosophers.
evidence_quote: attribute their uselessness to the fault of those who will not use them
rationale: The wise do not beg to command, as a pilot does not beg the crew.
argued_against: those who deem the best philosophers useless; mutinous rulers

recommendation: Do not give way to weakness; cast off the coward-fit and rise to fight.
evidence_quote: Forbid thyself to feebleness! it mars thy warrior-name! cast off the coward-fit!
rationale: Such weakness is shameful to the brave and bars the path of virtue.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not mourn for the living or the dead; the wise do not grieve.
evidence_quote: for the wise in heart mourn not for those that live, nor those that die
rationale: The Life never ceases to be: it is indestructible and only bodies perish.
argued_against: grieving where no grief should be

recommendation: Bear sorrow and joy, heat and cold, with a strong constant calm, as the wise do.
evidence_quote: Bear with it, Prince! As the wise bear.
rationale: Sense-life is brief and changeable; the soul unmoved by sorrow and joy lives the undying life.

recommendation: Fight; do not think you kill or are killed, since the spirit cannot be slain.
evidence_quote: Let them perish, Prince! and fight!
rationale: The spirit is birthless, deathless, and unchangeable; only fleeting bodies perish.
argued_against: thinking 'I have slain a man' or 'I am slain'

recommendation: Learn the truth that the Life is indestructible and spreads through all.
evidence_quote: To see this truth of both is theirs who part essence from accident
rationale: Spirit is endless, infinite, and cannot be diminished or changed.
argued_against: fearing death, confusing substance with shadow

recommendation: Train the best natures in arithmetic and do not give it up; make it a subject of education.
evidence_quote: arithmetic is a kind of knowledge in which the best natures should be trained, and which must not be given up
rationale: It is very difficult, and few studies are as hard.

recommendation: Have the inhabitants of the city learn geometry, as it draws the soul toward truth and eternal being.
evidence_quote: nothing should be more sternly laid down than that the inhabitants of your fair city should by all means learn geometry
rationale: Geometry draws the soul to truth and philosophy, and students of it learn faster in all subjects, with military advantages as well.
conditions: applies as knowledge of the eternal, not of what perishes
argued_against: treating geometry as only practical (squaring, extending, applying)

recommendation: Pursue geometry for knowledge, not for daily practical uses.
evidence_quote: knowledge is the real object of the whole science
rationale: The knowledge geometry aims at is of the eternal, not the perishing and transient.
argued_against: geometricians who confuse the needs of geometry with those of daily life

recommendation: Use the starry heavens only as a pattern for higher knowledge; study astronomy by reason, not by looking at the sky.
evidence_quote: The spangled heavens should be used as a pattern and with a view to that higher knowledge
rationale: True motions are apprehended by reason, not sight; gazing at the heavens makes the soul look downward.
argued_against: treating astronomy as the study of visible sense particulars

recommendation: The State should direct and honor the study of solid geometry so that it can advance.
evidence_quote: if the whole State became the director of these studies and gave honour to them
rationale: Without state patronage the subject lacks energy, directors, and humble students; with it, disciples would come and discoveries follow.
argued_against: neglect of these studies by government and conceited students

recommendation: See the difference between matter and spirit and between flesh and spirit.
evidence_quote: they who, by such eye of wisdom, see how Matter, and what deals with it, divide
rationale: The wise who see this go the way that leads to Life.

recommendation: Overcome Passion and Ignorance and live in Soothfastness, since the soul's fate follows the quality it dies in.
evidence_quote: Passion and Ignorance, once overcome, leave Soothfastness
rationale: Soothfastness leads upward, Passion to a middle place, Ignorance to lower deeps; their fruits are sweetness, pain, and darkness.

recommendation: Be even-minded toward the three Qualities and toward joy and grief, praise and blame, friend and foe, and detach from undertakings.
evidence_quote: he who with equanimity surveys lustre of goodness, strife of passion, sloth of ignorance
rationale: Such a person surmounts the Qualities and attains the Lord.
argued_against: being angry or wishful about the qualities; being swayed by praise and dispraise

recommendation: Adore the Lord with single, fervent faith.
evidence_quote: With single, fervent faith adoring Me
rationale: Such devotion passes beyond the Qualities to Brahma and the Lord.

recommendation: Whet the axe of detachment and cut the roots of sense-life, then worship the Highest always.
evidence_quote: The axe of sharp Detachment ye would whet
rationale: Actions bind people by ever-tightening bonds; detached ones reach the eternal world and never return.
scope: all who understand the teaching of the tree
argued_against: clinging to sense-life, passion, and dreams

recommendation: Know the Supreme and worship him with your whole soul.
evidence_quote: knoweth all, dear Prince! And with his whole soul ever worshippeth Me.
rationale: Who comprehends the mystery has wisdom and is quit of works in bliss.
argued_against: unenlightened and foolish ones who do not perceive the spirit

recommendation: Cultivate fearlessness, truthfulness, charity, tenderness to sufferers, humility, patience, purity, slowness to wrath, and harm nothing living; be neither revengeful nor proud.
evidence_quote: such be the signs, O Indian Prince! of him whose feet are set on that fair path which leads to heavenly birth
rationale: These are the signs of one on the path to heavenly birth.

recommendation: Do not go beyond or fall short of the due mean; both are wrong.
evidence_quote: To go beyond is as wrong as to fall short.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Serve your prince according to what is right, and retire if you cannot.
evidence_quote: one who serves his prince according to what is right, and when he finds he cannot do so, retires
rationale: none given
argued_against: mere ministers who serve without regard to right

recommendation: Learn to serve people and understand life before trying to serve spirits or understand death.
evidence_quote: While you are not able to serve men, how can you serve their spirits?
rationale: If you cannot serve men, you cannot serve spirits; if you do not know life, you cannot know death.

recommendation: Match advice to temperament: urge the slow forward and hold the energetic back before acting on what one hears.
evidence_quote: Ch'iu is retiring and slow; therefore, I urged him forward. Yu has more than his own share of energy
rationale: Different dispositions need opposite correction.
conditions: depends on whether one is slow or overly energetic

recommendation: Follow the men of former times in ceremonies and music.
evidence_quote: If I have occasion to use those things, I follow the men of former times.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not enrich the already wealthy by heavy taxation; such a person is no disciple.
evidence_quote: He is no disciple of mine. My little children, beat the drum and assail him.
rationale: none given
argued_against: collecting imposts to increase an already rich lord's wealth

recommendation: Love learning, as Yen Hui did.
evidence_quote: he loved to learn
rationale: none given

recommendation: Show ceremonious respect to mourners, the blind, and those in formal dress, and change countenance at sudden thunder or a feast of plenty.
evidence_quote: he would change countenance; when he saw any one wearing the cap of full dress, or a blind person
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
conditions: applies even in undress or toward acquaintances

recommendation: Do not accept a man as good merely because his discourse seems solid and sincere.
evidence_quote: If, because a man's discourse appears solid and sincere, we allow him to be a good man, is he really a superior man?
rationale: Gravity may be only appearance.

recommendation: A good lawgiver and physician should keep idle spendthrifts (drones) out of the city and cut them out quickly if they get in.
evidence_quote: keep them at a distance and prevent, if possible, their ever coming in
rationale: These classes are plagues of any city, like phlegm and bile in the body; in democracy drones almost run everything.
conditions: if they have already got in
argued_against: idle spendthrifts, stingless and stinging drones

recommendation: Do not live by the whim of the hour, with neither law nor order, and call that freedom.
evidence_quote: His life has neither law nor order; and this distracted existence he terms joy and bliss and freedom
rationale: Such a life is motley, shifting between drink, diet, exercise, idling, philosophy, and politics, with no steady aim.
argued_against: the democratic man indulging each appetite and calling it liberty

recommendation: Do not let the desire for freedom go without limit; excess of liberty passes into excess of slavery.
evidence_quote: The excess of liberty, whether in States or individuals, seems only to pass into excess of slavery.
rationale: Excess of anything often brings a reaction in the opposite direction; unlimited liberty breeds anarchy and then tyranny.
argued_against: insatiable thirst for freedom and impatience with authority

recommendation: Keep respect for parents, teachers, elders, rulers, and the laws; do not level all ranks.
evidence_quote: the father grows accustomed to descend to the level of his sons and to fear them
rationale: Leveling makes citizens chafe at all authority and disregard even the laws, opening the way to tyranny.
argued_against: fathers fearing sons, scholars despising masters, citizens disregarding laws

recommendation: Fix heart and thought on the Lord. Adore Him, bring Him offerings, and bow down to Him.
evidence_quote:
Fix heart and thought on Me! Adore Me! Bring
  Offerings to Me! Make Me prostrations!
rationale: Those who worship Him with love are in Him and He in them; devotion leads the spirit to His rest.
scope: all people, including those of low birth, women, and sinners

recommendation: Make the Lord your supreme joy.
evidence_quote:
Make
  Me your supremest joy!
rationale: Doing so, undivided, guides the spirit to His rest.

recommendation: Set your faith firmly on the Lord, trusting that no one who trusts Him can perish.
evidence_quote: set your faith fast on Me!
rationale: Those who trust Him cannot perish, and this world is fleeting and false.
argued_against: Treating this fleeting, false world as the object of faith

recommendation: Count even a person of evil life among the good once he turns his thought straight to the Lord.
evidence_quote:
If one of evil life turn in his thought
  Straightly to Me, count him amidst the good
rationale: Such a person has chosen the high way, will soon grow righteous, and will reach unchanging peace.
scope: anyone of evil life who turns to God, of any birth, sex, or caste
conditions: The person must turn wholeheartedly to the Lord
argued_against: Judging a repentant sinner as still evil

recommendation: Recognize the Lord as the source of all creatures and cleave to Him, with heart and breath fixed on Him and praising Him.
evidence_quote: The wise in spirit cleave to Me, into My Being brought;
rationale: Those who know Him as the source of all find happiness and peace, and He gives them a mind of perfect mood and dispels their ignorance.

recommendation: Discriminate the Supreme Truth, the real nature of the Self, and shake off the delusion your own mind created.
evidence_quote: Thou,  too,  discriminate
rationale: Doing so brings freedom, illumination, and the consummation of life.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: Delusion created by one's own mind

recommendation: Through Samadhi with a perfectly stilled mind, visualize the Truth of the Self with clear realization.
evidence_quote:
Through  Samadhi  in  which  the 
mind  has  been  perfectly  stilled,  visualise 
the  Truth  of  the  Self  with  the  eye  of  clear 
Realisation.
rationale: Once the meaning of the scriptural words heard from the Guru is perfectly discerned, no more doubt arises.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Realize your identity with Brahman, so that no further rebirth follows.
evidence_quote:
For  one  who  has  realised  the  Truth 
of  Brahman  there  is  no  more  transmigra
rationale: For one who has realized the Truth of Brahman there is no more transmigration; all accumulated actions come to nought.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: Seeing oneself as the body, with outgoing senses

recommendation: Do not cling to unreal objects or the dream-world of appearances.
evidence_quote:
If  he  still  clings  to 
those  nnrcal  objects,  he  is  emphatically 
declared  to  be  not  yet  free  from  sleep.
rationale: One who still clings to unreal objects is not yet awake and not free.

recommendation: Stay the same in mind whether your body is honored by the good or tormented by the wicked.
evidence_quote:
He  who  feels  just  the  same  when 
his  body  is  either  worshipped  by  the  good 
or  tormented  by  the  wicked
rationale: This is the mark of one liberated in life.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: seekers aspiring to be liberated in life

recommendation: Give up all attachment and sense-enjoyments, be purified and restrained, so as to realize the Supreme Truth.
evidence_quote:
High-souled  Sannyasins  who  have 
got  rid  of  all  attachment
rationale: Such Sannyasins realize the Supreme Truth and at the end attain Supreme Bliss.

recommendation: Be patient under suffering and do not give way to impatience or grief.
evidence_quote:
to be patient under suffering is best, and that
we should not give way to impatience
rationale: No one knows whether such things are good or evil, nothing is gained by impatience, no human thing is of serious importance, and grief hinders what is needed.
scope: all people, especially the good man facing loss
conditions: Even a good man cannot help sorrowing but should moderate it, especially in public

recommendation: After misfortune, take counsel and order your affairs as reason judges best, and apply a remedy to the soul at once.
evidence_quote:
take counsel about what has happened, and when the dice
have been thrown order our affairs in the way which reason deems best
rationale: This is the true way of meeting the attacks of fortune; what is most required at such moments is deliberation.
argued_against: Behaving like children who hold the struck part and howl

recommendation: Do not waste time wailing over what has struck you, as children do.
evidence_quote:
not, like children who have had a fall, keeping hold of the part struck
and wasting time in setting up a howl
rationale: Lamentation wastes time and is irrational, useless, and cowardly.
argued_against: Lamentation and endless recollection of one's troubles

recommendation: Trust measuring, numbering, and weighing over appearances; let the rational part of the soul govern.
evidence_quote:
the better part of the soul is likely to be that which trusts to
measure and calculation
rationale: Measure and calculation correct the illusions of sight, and the part that opposes them is inferior.
argued_against: Being ruled by illusion and appearance

recommendation: Do not rely on a probability drawn from analogy; examine the question further.
evidence_quote:
Do not rely, I said, on a probability derived from the analogy of
painting; but let us examine further
rationale: none given

recommendation: Be wary of imitative art and poetry that appeals to the passionate, irrational part of the soul.
evidence_quote: they have no true or healthy aim
rationale: Imitation is far from truth, allied with the irrational part of the soul, and the popular poet prefers the passionate, fitful temper because it is easy to imitate.
scope: viewers and audiences of imitative art, especially poetry and theatre
argued_against: Imitative poets who aim at popularity

recommendation: Frequently consider the connection of all things in the universe and how they relate to one another.
evidence_quote:
Frequently consider the connection of all things in the universe and
their relation to one another.
rationale: All things are implicated with one another through the unity of substance.

recommendation: Adapt yourself to the circumstances of your lot, and love the people among whom you live, sincerely.
evidence_quote:
Adapt thyself to the things with which thy lot has been cast: and
the men among whom thou hast received thy portion, love them, but do it
truly
rationale: none given

recommendation: Reverence the power within you that made you, and live and act according to its will.
evidence_quote:
the more is it fit
to reverence this power
rationale: If you live and act according to it, everything in you conforms to intelligence.

recommendation: Judge only what is in your power to be good or bad, so you have no reason to blame the gods or hate people.
evidence_quote:
if we judge only those things which are in our
power to be good or bad, there remains no reason either for finding
fault with God or standing in a hostile attitude to man.
rationale: Treating outside things as good or evil makes you blame the gods and hate those who cause loss, which is unjust.
argued_against: Treating things outside our power as good or evil, and blaming gods or men

recommendation: Understand what kind of co-worker you make yourself in the universe's work, and do not be a mean and ridiculous part.
evidence_quote:
It remains then for thee to understand among what
kind of workmen thou placest thyself
rationale: All people work toward one end, and the ruler of all makes right use of each.
argued_against: Finding fault with events and opposing or hindering what happens

recommendation: Accept with pleasure and contentment what happens in the general order of things.
evidence_quote:
I ought to
accept with pleasure and to be content with them
rationale: If the gods decided about me, they decided well; if only about the whole, my events follow from that arrangement; if about nothing, I can decide what is useful.
argued_against: Believing the gods decide nothing or intend harm

recommendation: Treat as useful to you only what is useful to your city and to the world.
evidence_quote:
The things then which are useful to these cities
are alone useful to me.
rationale: My nature is rational and social, and my country is Rome as a Roman but the world as a man.

recommendation: Pass your life in truth and justice, with a benevolent disposition even toward liars and unjust people.
evidence_quote:
One
thing here is worth a great deal, to pass thy life in truth and justice,
with a benevolent disposition even to liars and unjust men.
rationale: All people and their pursuits come to dust, so only this is worth much.
argued_against: Hostility toward liars and the unjust

recommendation: Think continually that all kinds of people and pursuits are dead and gone.
evidence_quote:
Think continually that all kinds of men and all kinds of pursuits
and of all nations are dead
rationale: Even the great orators, philosophers, and rulers are long in the dust, so death does no harm to them.

recommendation: When you want delight, think of the virtues of those who live with you and keep them before you.
evidence_quote:
When thou wishest to delight thyself, think of the virtues of those
who live with thee
rationale: Nothing delights so much as examples of virtue in those around us.

recommendation: Do not be dissatisfied that you live only so many years; be content with your time.
evidence_quote:
Be not dissatisfied then that thou
must live only so many years and not more
rationale: You are satisfied with the weight assigned to you, so be content with your assigned time too.
argued_against: Discontent with the length of life

recommendation: Try to persuade others, but act on justice even against their will; if force blocks you, stay content and turn the obstacle to another virtue.
evidence_quote:
Let us try to persuade them [men]. But act even against their will,
when the principles of justice lead that way.
rationale: Your attempt was conditional and you did not desire impossibilities, so you reach your aim.
conditions: When someone uses force to block you, shift to contentment and tranquility

recommendation: Take your own acts, not others' activity or your sensations, as your good.
evidence_quote:
he who has
understanding considers his own acts to be his own good.
rationale: The fame-lover places his good in others' activity and the pleasure-lover in his sensations.

recommendation: Form no opinion about outside things and do not let your soul be disturbed.
evidence_quote:
It is in our power to have no opinion about a thing, and not to be
disturbed in our soul
rationale: Things themselves have no natural power to form our judgments.

recommendation: Attend carefully to what others say and, as far as possible, enter the speaker's mind.
evidence_quote:
Accustom thyself to attend carefully to what is said by another, and
as much as it is possible, be in the speaker's mind.
rationale: none given
conditions: As far as it is possible

recommendation: Remember that what harms the community is not good for the individual.
evidence_quote:
That which is not good for the swarm, neither is it good for the
bee.
rationale: The individual and the whole share one good.
argued_against: Pursuing private good against the community

recommendation: Do not make war; war does not solve questions and sows the seeds of another war.
evidence_quote: War does not solve any question.
rationale: The slayer gets a slayer, the conqueror a conqueror, the despoiler is despoiled in turn.
argued_against: The resolution to wage war on the Koliyas

recommendation: Recognize that enmity does not end through enmity; conquer it with love only.
evidence_quote:
Dharma, as I understand it,
            consists in recognising that enmity does not disappear
            by enmity. It can be conquered by love only.
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Investigate carefully who is the guilty party before declaring war, and admit your own side's blame.
evidence_quote:
Careful investigation should be made to
ascertain who is the guilty party.
rationale: Their own men have also been aggressors, so they are not free from blame.

recommendation: Settle disputes by arbitration with a panel chosen by both sides.
evidence_quote:
I therefore propose
that we elect two men from us and the Koliyas should
be asked to elect two from them and the four should
elect a fifth person and these should settle the dispute.
rationale: We are not completely free from blame.

recommendation: Do not destroy close relations in war.
evidence_quote:
The Sakyas and the Koliyas are close relations. It is
unwise that they should destroy each other.
rationale: Close relations destroying each other is unwise.
argued_against: Claim that Kshatriyas must fight even brothers

recommendation: Each class should perform its own duty; Kshatriyas must fight even against brothers.
evidence_quote: fighting is the duty of the Kshatriyas
rationale: There is merit in each class performing its duty; such is the injunction of the Shastras.
scope: members of each class; Kshatriyas in war

recommendation: Obey the majority decision of the assembly and keep the vows taken on joining.
evidence_quote: You must obey the majority decision of the Sangh.
rationale: Breaking vows exposes one to public shame, social boycott, and confiscation of family lands.

recommendation: Put the best interests of the community above public shame, and refuse to join a war you judge harmful.
evidence_quote:
What is public shame
to me before the best interests of the Sakyas ?
rationale: The war would give the Kosala king a handle to reduce Sakya freedom further.
argued_against: Silent compliance by the minority who lacked courage

recommendation: Let the guilty alone bear the penalty; do not punish innocent family members.
evidence_quote: Please do not punish my family.
rationale: They are innocent; the one who opposed is the one at fault.
argued_against: Social boycott and confiscation of land against the innocent

recommendation: Give up fear; there is a means of crossing the sea of relative existence.
evidence_quote:
Fear  not,  O  learned  one,  there  is 
no  death  for  thee
rationale: There is no death for you; sages have crossed over by a sovereign means, which the teacher will teach.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
conditions: The seeker has sought refuge, thirsts for liberation, obeys scripture, and has a pacified mind

recommendation: Abide in faith, devotion, and the Yoga of meditation.
evidence_quote:
Faith,  devotion  and  the  Yoga  of 
meditation
rationale: The Sruti names these as the immediate factors of Liberation from bondage.

recommendation: Strive personally, by every means in your power, to be free from the bondage of repeated births and deaths.
evidence_quote:
the  wise  should,  as  in 
the  case  of  disease  and  the  like,  personally 
strive  by  all  the  means  in  their  power
rationale: Others cannot remove your bondage, just as only the patient who takes diet and medicine recovers.

recommendation: Seek the realization of your identity with Brahman, since liberation comes by no other means.
evidence_quote:
Neither  by  Yoga,  nor  by  Sankhya, 
nor  .by  work,  nor  by  learning.,  but  by  the 
realisation  of  one's  identity  with  Brah
rationale: none given
argued_against: Relying on Yoga, Sankhya, work, or learning alone

recommendation: Earnestly set about knowing the true nature of the Self rather than getting lost in the many words of the Scriptures.
evidence_quote:
the  man  of 
wisdom  should  earnestly  set  about  knowing 
the  true  nature  of  the  Self
rationale: Scripture study is useless until the highest Truth is known, and the many words are a dense forest where the mind rambles.
argued_against: Scriptural erudition and skill in exposition as ends

recommendation: Do not rely on merely uttering the word Brahman; seek direct realization.
evidence_quote:
without 
direct  realisation  one  cannot  be  liberated 
by  the  mere  utterance  of  the  word  Brah
rationale: Naming a medicine does not cure a disease, and calling an emperor's title does not make one emperor.
argued_against: Mere verbal repetition and perverted argumentation

recommendation: Learn from a knower of Brahman, then reflect and meditate; do not use perverted argument.
evidence_quote:
but  not  through 
perverted  argumentations.
rationale: A hidden treasure needs instruction, excavation, and grasping; it never comes out by being called by name.

recommendation: Feel extreme aversion to perishable things, then develop calmness, self-control, and forbearance, then hear, reflect, and meditate constantly.
evidence_quote:
The  first  step  to  Liberation  is  the 
extreme  aversion  to  all  perishable  things, 
then  follow  calmness,  self-control,  for
rationale: After these steps the learned one attains the supreme Nirvikalpa state and realizes Nirvana in this life.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Listen attentively to the teacher and decide in your own mind about the Self and non-Self.
evidence_quote:
Listen  attentively,  O  learned  one, 
to  what  I  am  going  to  say.
rationale: By listening you shall be instantly free from the bondage of Samsara.

recommendation: Help others out of trouble without any motive, as the good and magnanimous do.
evidence_quote: It  is  the  very  nature  of  the  magnani
rationale: The magnanimous help others cross the ocean of birth and death, as the moon cools the parched earth.

recommendation: Devoutly hear or recite the tale of the Lord's deeds and marriage.
evidence_quote:
All  pious  souls,  that 
devoutly  hear  or  recite  the  auspicious  festivities
rationale: Those who hear it attain everlasting felicity, steady devotion, and lasting happiness by the Lord's favour.
conditions: Hearing must be done with love and reverence

recommendation: Love Hari's feet wholeheartedly, discard all vanities, and awake from the darkness of delusion.
evidence_quote: Have  a  hearty  love  for  Hari's  feet,  discarding  all  vanities
rationale: Much time has been spent in sleep; love of the Lord extinguishes the fire of covetousness.

recommendation: In faith, meditate upon Hari as the one remedy for evil times and a stained body.
evidence_quote:
he  only  is  wise  who  so  thinketh  and  in 
faith  meditates  upon  Hari
rationale: The times are evil and the body is stained with filth; there is but one remedy.

recommendation: Honor Brahmans, the gods, your guru, and your parents, and receive their blessing.
evidence_quote:
The  four  brothers 
saluted  the
rationale: The text presents the brothers as models; blessings are received gladly.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: not stated; shown through the brothers

recommendation: Keep the customary ablutions, bathing, and morning devotions, even when already pure.
evidence_quote:
they  performed 
all  the  customary  ablutions  and  bathed  in  the  holy  river 
and  completed  their  morning  devotions
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: not stated; shown through the brothers
conditions: They did so though pure in themselves

recommendation: Honor your guru and credit his favor for your protection and knowledge.
evidence_quote:
by  your  guru's  blessing

you  acquired  all    knowledge
rationale: The saint's favor averted calamities and gave all knowledge.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Know that the Self is untouched by the body and its changes, as the sky is untouched by the jar.
evidence_quote:
Let  this  inert  body  drop  down  in 
water  or  on  land,  I  am  not  touched  by  its 
properties
rationale: The activity of the supervening adjunct is wrongly ascribed to the Self, as a reflection's movement is ascribed to the sun.
argued_against: Thinking 'I am the doer', 'I am the enjoyer', 'I am killed'

recommendation: See the universe as nothing but Brahman, with the eye of illumination and a serene mind, under all circumstances.
evidence_quote:
See  this-  with  the  eye  of  illr&mination  and 
a  serene  mind,  under  all  circumstances.
rationale: The universe is an unbroken series of perceptions of Brahman, just as a seeing person sees nothing but forms.
argued_against: Seeing the world as separate from Brahman

recommendation: Do not give up the Supreme Bliss for unsubstantial things.
evidence_quote: What  wise  man  would  discard  that
rationale: Unreal things give neither satisfaction nor an end to misery; no one would look at a painted moon when the real moon shines.

recommendation: Be satisfied with the realization of Bliss Absolute and live happily in identity with Brahman.
evidence_quote:
live 
happily  in  a  state  of  identity  with  the 
Real  Brahman.
rationale: Perceiving unreal things brings neither satisfaction nor an end to misery.

recommendation: Behold and think of the Self alone in all circumstances, enjoy its Bliss, and pass your time so.
evidence_quote: pass  thy  time,  O  noble  soul!
rationale: none given

recommendation: Always identify yourself with the Bliss Absolute and remain quiet.
evidence_quote:
always  identifying  thyself  with  the 
Bliss  Absolute
rationale: Dualistic conceptions in the Atman are like castles in the air; identification brings Supreme Peace.

recommendation: Be neither grieved nor elated by sense-objects, neither attached nor averse to them.
evidence_quote:
is  neither  grieved,  nor  elated  by 
sense-objects
rationale: The man of realization is satisfied with constant Bliss and so takes pleasure in the Self.

recommendation: Pray to Hari (the Lord); without prayer, salvation and release from the troubles of existence are not possible.
evidence_quote:
without  prayer  to  Hari,  the 
troubles  incident  to  existence  cannot  be  dispersed
rationale: Troubles of existence cannot be dispersed without prayer; even the wisest hoping for salvation without it is like a beast without tail and horns. Illusion yields only to the Lord's help.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: Those who hope for salvation without prayer, even the wisest of men.

recommendation: Value faith above all other virtues and blessings; without faith and prayer they are worth little.
evidence_quote: Without  faith  what  are  any  virtues  or  blessings
rationale: Without faith, virtues and blessings are like condiments without salt; no good is of avail without prayer.
argued_against: Seeking powers, wealth, or knowledge without faith.

recommendation: By means of a regulated mind and purified intellect, realize your own Self directly and identify yourself with it.
evidence_quote:
realise  thou 
directly  thy  own  Self
rationale: This allows you to cross the ocean of birth and death and be established in Brahman and blessed.
conditions: Requires a regulated mind and a purified intellect.
argued_against: Identifying oneself with the body and the non-self.

recommendation: Do not identify the Self with the non-self (the body); doing so is bondage.
evidence_quote:
is  due  to  his  ignorance,  and  brings  in  its 
train  the  miseries  of  birth  and  death
rationale: Identifying with the perishable body is due to ignorance, binds one like a caterpillar in its cocoon, and brings the miseries of birth and death.
argued_against: Treating the evanescent body as real and nourishing it with sense-objects.

recommendation: Know the body, mind, universe, and Maya to be non-self and therefore unreal, like a mirage.
evidence_quote:
know  thou  to  be 
Non-self  and  therefore  unreal
rationale: Everything from Mahat to the gross body is an effect of Maya and so unreal like a mirage in a desert.

recommendation: Avoid lust, anger, avarice, arrogance, spite, egoism, envy, and jealousy, the attributes of Rajas.
evidence_quote: the  dire  attributes  of  Rajas
rationale: These qualities of Rajas produce the worldly tendency of man, so Rajas is a cause of bondage.
argued_against: Lust, anger, avarice, arrogance, spite, egoism, envy, and jealousy.

recommendation: Master your passions, purify yourself, and restrain your body; this makes the true saint.
evidence_quote: who has cut off his passions and purified himself
rationale: none given

recommendation: Make your wealth known to the poor by giving; be liberal and generous.
evidence_quote: To what end is wealth if unknown to the poor
rationale: Wealth, a relation's prosperity, and a physician are useless if they do not reach the poor or sick; the virtuous giver's wealth keeps flowing like a wellspring.
argued_against: Wealthy people who show no liberality.

recommendation: Judge nobility by liberality, not by size or looks.
evidence_quote: devoid of liberality he is no noble
rationale: A man without liberality is no noble however large, like a buffalo compared with an elephant.
argued_against: Valuing stature or beard over generosity.

recommendation: Do not raise the hopes of the poor and then send them away empty-handed.
evidence_quote: Those who first excite hopes in the poor
rationale: Such hard misers will feel the effect of the poor's sighs, lose their hopes, and perish.
argued_against: Hard misers who raise the hopes of the poor and then refuse them.

recommendation: Do not be puffed up with pride; the soul will leave the body unknown to anyone.
evidence_quote:
he 
is a madman who, unconscious of the degradation he shall 
meet in death, is puffed up with pride
rationale: The soul will depart one day, and you will face degradation in death.

recommendation: Do good during life, since good deeds are the only possession that remains after death.
evidence_quote:
the good 
he has done will be his only possession
rationale: At death wife, sons, and connections do not follow; only the soul and the good one has done remain.

recommendation: Keep your word; one who breaks it is viler than a low-born person.
evidence_quote: he who breaks his word is far viler
rationale: Those who give their word and break it are lost to shame; a promise-breaker is far viler than a Pariar by birth.

recommendation: Do not grieve a friend once you have made friendship with him.
evidence_quote:
cruel 
is he who, after contracting friendship, grieves his friend
rationale: none given
argued_against: Those who grieve a friend after contracting friendship; also those who disregard distress.

recommendation: Guard the charitable gifts of others and do not embezzle them.
evidence_quote:
but if thou embezzle the 
alms of others, thy own charities shall become fruitless
rationale: Guarding others' benefactions doubles the merit of your own charities, while embezzling alms makes your own charities fruitless.

recommendation: Do not regard someone as degraded because of birth; understanding makes the noblest, and do not reproach the low-born.
evidence_quote:
Consider not him a Pariar of degraded rank who 
is so by birth
rationale: The man of understanding is of the noblest tribe; one who reproaches a Pariar is worse than he.
argued_against: Judging people by birth, and reproaching the low-born.

recommendation: Do not associate with the vile or admit low-minded people into your house.
evidence_quote:
If he joins himself to the vile, and associates 
with him, he will be ruined
rationale: Joining the vile ruins whoever one is, like drinking milk under a palm tree; a low-minded wretch in the house brings lament, like a fly in the stomach.
argued_against: Associating with the vile and low-minded.

recommendation: Do not leave your brothers because of a quarrelsome wife.
evidence_quote:
listening to his fractious wife, 
quits his brothers and separates himself from them
rationale: Relying on a fractious wife against one's brothers is like trying to swim the Godavery holding a dog's tail.
argued_against: Following a fractious wife in abandoning one's brothers.

recommendation: Do not serve a senseless prince or beg from a miser; you will gain nothing.
evidence_quote:
However long you serve a prince void of sense 
you will gain no living
rationale: Serving a senseless prince yields only expectations, like stroking a dry cow's udder; begging from a miser gets no milk.
argued_against: Serving senseless rulers and begging from misers.

recommendation: Give up every other object, seek happiness alone, and trust God with full reliance; this faith brings perfection.
evidence_quote: trusts in Thee with full reliance
rationale: By such faith one will gain perfection.

recommendation: Guard against lust and the pursuit of women; desire blinds men and brings troubles.
evidence_quote:
this strong cupidity plunges us in 
unspeakable troubles
rationale: Desire for women blinds men to their destiny, seizes them with madness, and plunges them into unspeakable troubles.
argued_against: Unrestrained desire for women; lustful men who cannot be taught mildness.

recommendation: Accept that what is destined will happen and what is not doomed will never befall you.
evidence_quote:
How should all that is destined to happen fail of 
occurring
rationale: The ruling power is independent of ourselves.

recommendation: Do not covet wealth that is not yours, however large the pile.
evidence_quote:
will not touch 
it
rationale: none given
scope: the man of pure birth who is rich in himself

recommendation: Be dispassionate, both internally and externally.
evidence_quote:
for  thy  welfare,  be 
dispassionate
rationale: For the self-controlled man dispassion is the best instrument of happiness; with pure realization of the Self it brings independence and is the gateway to liberation.

recommendation: Always fix your mind on the eternal Self.
evidence_quote:
always  fix  thy  mind  on  the  eternal 
Self
rationale: This is for your welfare and leads to liberation.

recommendation: Sever your craving for sense-objects, which are like poison.
