evidence_quote: Sever  thy  craving  for  sense-objects
rationale: Craving for sense-objects is the very image of death.

recommendation: Give up pride of caste, family, and order of life.
evidence_quote:
giving  up  thy  pride 
of  caste,  family  and  order  of  life
rationale: You are really the Witness, Brahman, unshackled by the mind.
argued_against: Pride of caste, family, and order of life.

recommendation: Fling actions to a distance; give up identification with the body and other unreal things.
evidence_quote:
fling 
actions  to  a  distance
rationale: You are really the Witness, Brahman, and these things are unreal.
argued_against: Identifying with the body and similar unreal things.

recommendation: Do not hold regard for the body; think of yourself as pure and immovable.
evidence_quote:
So  long  as  man  has  any  regard  for 
this  corpse-like  body,  he  is  impure
rationale: While one regards the body he is impure and suffers enemies, birth, death, and disease; thinking of oneself as pure frees him from them.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Fix the mind on Brahman, restrain the senses, and always drink joyfully of the Bliss of Brahman in your own Self.
evidence_quote:
always  drink  joyfully  of  the 
Bliss  of  Brahman  in  thy  own  Self
rationale: Other things pursued as means of happiness are entirely hollow.
conditions: Held with steady body and restrained senses.
argued_against: Pursuing other things as means of happiness.

recommendation: Reflect continuously on the Atman, with no foreign thought intervening, and realize it as your own real Self.
evidence_quote:
one  must  distinctly  realise  It 
to  be  one's  own  real  Self
rationale: none given

recommendation: First destroy the hopes raised by egoism in the gross body, then in the subtle body; realize Brahman as your Self and live as Brahman.
evidence_quote:
destroy  the  hopes  raised  by 
egoism  in  this  filthy  gross  body
rationale: none given

recommendation: Treat prosperity and adversity alike; do not triumph in the one or be downcast in the other, as fools do.
evidence_quote: wise  men  account  both  alike
rationale: Life and death, pleasure and pain, loss and gain are governed by time and fate as unalterably as day and night.
argued_against: Fools who triumph in prosperity and are downcast in adversity.

recommendation: Take courage and cease vain regrets, since the good of all depends on you.
evidence_quote: cease  vain  regrets
rationale: Everything is governed by fate; if you have courage you will get across, otherwise the whole family will be drowned.
scope: a ruler or leader in calamity

recommendation: Do not forget sound polity; cherish your subjects in word, thought, and deed.
evidence_quote:
Cherish  your 
subjects  in  word,  thought  and  deed
rationale: none given
conditions: Applies now that he has the royal dignity.

recommendation: Be obedient to all the queen mothers without partiality.
evidence_quote:
be  obedient  to  all 
the  queen-mothers  without  partiality
rationale: none given
scope: the younger brother who becomes king

recommendation: Fulfil your duty as a brother and be dutiful to father, mother, and kindred.
evidence_quote:
Fulfil  your  duty, 
brother,  as  a  brother
rationale: none given
scope: the younger brother who becomes king

recommendation: Value as best friend the one who ensures the king's happiness.
evidence_quote:
He  is 
my  best  friend  who  ensures  the  king's  happiness
rationale: none given

recommendation: Do not mourn for the one who goes into exile; see it as pleasant and meritorious.
evidence_quote: mourn  not  for  me
rationale: The exile is pleasant and profitable to the son, and a grace and meritorious deed on the father's part.
scope: a father whose son is exiled

recommendation: Meditate on Brahman, the pure, infinite, changeless reality, as your own Self: "That Brahman art thou."
evidence_quote:
that 
Brahman  art  thou,  meditate  on  this  in 
thy  mind
rationale: Brahman is the substratum of the universe and one's own Self; the Vedas establish the identity of Jiva and Brahman.

recommendation: Dismiss the phantom of the objective world that you have accepted as your own self, and realize your own Self by purified understanding.
evidence_quote:
dismiss  this  mere  phantom  of  an 
objective
rationale: The world is imagined and unreal, like a snake seen in a rope or like dreams.
argued_against: Taking the objective world as one's self.

recommendation: Eliminate the objective world by reasoning, then realize the oneness underlying Isvara and Jiva.
evidence_quote:
Perfectly 
eliminating  the  objective  world  in  this  way 
by  means  of  reasoning
rationale: Gross and subtle universes are imagined and not real.

recommendation: Reason out the identity of Isvara and Jiva by a method combining rejection and retention of their meanings; neither wholesale rejection nor wholesale retention works.
evidence_quote:
One  must  reason  out  through 
the  process  which  combines  the  two
rationale: The terms have contradictory literal attributes; only their implied meanings, the essence of Knowledge Absolute, are identical.
argued_against: Wholesale rejection or wholesale retention of the terms.

recommendation: Meditate on this truth yourself, using the recognized arguments.
evidence_quote:
one  must  oneself  meditate  in  one's  mind,  by 
means  of  the  recognised  arguments
rationale: By this one realizes the truth free from doubt, like water in the palm of one's hand.

recommendation: Do not see the universe as separate from the Supreme Self; its perceived separateness is false.
evidence_quote: perception  of  its  separateness  is  false
rationale: A superimposed attribute has no meaning apart from its substratum; the universe is Brahman seen through delusion.
argued_against: Perceiving the universe as separate from Brahman.

recommendation: Aim to prevent disputes so that the people have no litigations, rather than only settling them.
evidence_quote:
What is necessary, however, is to cause the people
to have no litigations
rationale: The Master says he hears cases like anyone else; the real task is prevention.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Govern by keeping affairs before the mind without weariness and practicing them with undeviating consistency.
evidence_quote:
to keep its affairs before the mind
without weariness, and to practise them with undeviating
consistency
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Study widely and restrain yourself with the rules of propriety, so as not to stray from what is right.
evidence_quote:
extensively studying all
learning, and keeping himself under the restraint of the rules of
propriety
rationale: This way one may not err from what is right.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Seek to perfect the admirable qualities of others, not their bad qualities.
evidence_quote:
The superior man seeks to
perfect the admirable qualities of men, and does not seek to perfect
their bad qualities
rationale: The superior man does this; the mean man does the opposite.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: The mean man, who perfects others' bad qualities.

recommendation: Lead the people with correctness; a ruler's own correct conduct makes orders unnecessary.
evidence_quote:
If you lead on the
people with correctness, who will dare not to be correct
rationale: To govern is to rectify; when the prince's conduct is correct, government is effective without orders, and if not, orders are not followed.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: Rulers whose own conduct is incorrect.

recommendation: Do not be covetous; a ruler's lack of greed stops theft among the people.
evidence_quote:
If you, sir, were not covetous, although you
should reward them to do it, they would not steal
rationale: If the ruler were not covetous, the people would not steal even if rewarded.

recommendation: Do not use killing in government; show desires for what is good, and the people will be good.
evidence_quote:
Let your evinced
desires be for what is good, and the people will be good
rationale: Inferiors bend to superiors like grass bends when the wind blows across it.
argued_against: Killing the unprincipled for the good of the principled.

recommendation: Be solid, straightforward, and a lover of righteousness; examine people's words and looks, and humble yourself to others.
evidence_quote:
the man of distinction is solid and straightforward,
and loves righteousness
rationale: Such a man will be distinguished in the country and in his clan.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: The man of mere notoriety, who assumes the appearance of virtue.

recommendation: Do not merely assume the appearance of virtue while acting against it, and do not seek notoriety instead of real distinction.
evidence_quote:
he assumes the appearance of

virtue, but his actions are opposed to it
rationale: The man of notoriety is heard of, but without any doubts about himself he rests in a false character.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Make doing what is to be done the first business and success secondary; this exalts virtue.
evidence_quote:
If doing what is to be done be made the first business, and
success a secondary consideration
rationale: This is the way to exalt virtue.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Attack your own wickedness and not that of others; this corrects cherished evil.
evidence_quote:
To assail one's own wickedness and not assail that of
others
rationale: This is the way to correct cherished evil.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not let a morning's anger make you disregard your own life and endanger your parents.
evidence_quote:
For a
morning's anger to disregard one's own life, and involve that of his
parents
rationale: Such behavior is a case of delusion.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Love all men; this is benevolence.
evidence_quote: It is to love all men
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Know all men; this is knowledge.
evidence_quote: It is to know all men
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Employ the upright and put aside the crooked; this can make the crooked upright.
evidence_quote:
Employ the upright and put aside all the
crooked
rationale: Examples: a sage-king selected a worthy man and all who were devoid of virtue disappeared.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Faithfully admonish your friend and lead him on skillfully; if he proves impracticable, stop so as not to disgrace yourself.
evidence_quote: Faithfully admonish your friend, and skillfully lead him on
rationale: Persisting after failure would disgrace yourself.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
conditions: Stop if the friend is impracticable.

recommendation: Meet with friends on grounds of culture, so that their friendship helps your virtue.
evidence_quote:
by their
friendship helps his virtue
rationale: Friendship helps virtue.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Go before the people with your example, be laborious in their affairs, and do not weary of it.
evidence_quote:
Go before the people with your example, and be laborious in their
affairs
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Employ your officers first, pardon small faults, and raise to office men of virtue and talents, starting with those you know.
evidence_quote:
pardon small faults, and
raise to office men of virtue and talents
rationale: Those you do not know will not be neglected by others.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Show cautious reserve about what you do not know.
evidence_quote:
A superior
man, in regard to what he does not know, shows a cautious reserve
rationale: Incorrect names ruin language, affairs, rites, punishments, and finally the people's footing.

recommendation: Use words and names correctly so that what you say can be carried out; let there be nothing incorrect in your words.
evidence_quote:
What the superior man
requires, is just that in his words there may be nothing incorrect
rationale: If names are incorrect, language does not fit the truth of things, affairs fail, and the people do not know how to move hand or foot.

recommendation: A superior should love propriety, righteousness, and good faith; then the people will be reverent, submissive, and sincere.
evidence_quote:
If a superior love propriety, the people will not dare not to
be reverent
rationale: The people will come from all quarters, so the ruler needs no knowledge of husbandry.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Learning must be put to practical use in government and missions; mere recitation is not enough.
evidence_quote:
of what practical use is
it
rationale: A man who can recite the odes but cannot act in office or reply unassisted on a mission gains nothing from his learning.

recommendation: Enrich the people first.
evidence_quote: Enrich them
rationale: A numerous people calls for more being done for them.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: After enriching the people, teach them.
evidence_quote: Teach them
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
conditions: Comes after the people have been enriched.

recommendation: Do not indulge in the eccentricities of folly (vanity, presumption, caprice, obstinacy, and one-sidedness).
evidence_quote:
Do  not  indulge  in  the  Eccentricities  of 
Folly
rationale: Deformity of mind is more obnoxious than that of the body; such people lack self-control and blind themselves with imaginary applause.
argued_against: Vain, presumptuous, capricious, obstinate, whimsical, sectarian, and one-sided people.

recommendation: Be more careful not to miss once than to hit a hundred times; avoid falling into error.
evidence_quote:
Be  more  careful  not  to  Miss  once  than  to 
Hit  a  hundred  times
rationale: People notice what goes wrong, not what goes right; one blemish outweighs all exploits.
argued_against: Ignoring that ill-will notices every error and no success.

recommendation: Keep something in reserve; do not use all your capacity and power at once.
evidence_quote: In  all  Things  keep  Something  in  Reserve
rationale: It keeps up your importance and gives you something to resort to when defeat is feared; the reserve is more important than the attacking force.

recommendation: Do not waste influence on little things; reserve the great as friends for great occasions.
evidence_quote:
One  should  not  make  use  of  great  confidence  for 
little  things
rationale: If you use up the great for little ends, nothing remains; a protector is valuable and a favour costs much.

recommendation: Keep the favour of the mighty; it matters more than goods and chattels.
evidence_quote:
more  important  to  keep  the  favour  of  the 
mighty  than  goods  and  chattels
rationale: Favour can make or unmake a whole world, and luck is generally envious of the wise.

recommendation: Never contend with a man who has nothing to lose; do not expose a valuable reputation to such risk.
evidence_quote:
Never  contend  with  a  Man  who  has  nothing 
to  Lose
rationale: The contest is unequal: he has no shame or fear of loss and resorts to insolence, while years of reputation can be lost in a moment.
conditions: If you must contend, enter with the greatest caution and retire in time.
argued_against: Contending with people who have lost everything including shame.

recommendation: Do not be glass (too easily offended) in intercourse, and still less in friendship.
evidence_quote: Do  not  be  Glass  in  Intercourse
rationale: Such people show inconsistency, imagine offences and oppressive intentions, are egoistic slaves of mood, and force others to treat them with great delicacy.

recommendation: Do not live in a hurry; be slow in enjoyment and quick at work.
evidence_quote: Do  not  live  in  a  Hurry
rationale: Hurried people run through pleasures without enjoying them and finish fortune sooner than life; work ends with pleasure, pleasure ends in regret.
argued_against: Living in a hurry like postilions of life.

recommendation: Be solid and truthful; avoid deceit and lies, for only truth gives true reputation and only reality real profit.
evidence_quote:
Only  Truth  can  give  true 
reputation
rationale: One deceit needs many others, so the whole house is built in the air and soon falls; unfounded things never reach old age.
argued_against: Deceivers and those who prefer a promising lie to the truth.

recommendation: Have knowledge, or know those who do; seek advice and take counsel with reason.
evidence_quote: to  ask  advice  proves  you  well  advised
rationale: True life is impossible without intelligence, one's own or another's; seeking advice does not lessen greatness and avoids defeat.
argued_against: Those who do not know that they do not know and think themselves wise.

recommendation: Avoid familiarities in intercourse; neither use them nor permit them.
evidence_quote: Avoid  Familiarities  in  Intercourse
rationale: Familiarity loses superiority and respect and breeds contempt; it is dangerous with superiors, unbecoming with inferiors, and worst with the common herd.

recommendation: Trust your heart, especially when it has been proved; never deny it a hearing.
evidence_quote:
Never 
deny  it  a  hearing
rationale: The heart is a house oracle that often foretells the most important things; many perished because they feared their own heart.
conditions: Especially when the heart has been proved.
argued_against: Fearing one's own heart without a better remedy.

recommendation: Practice reticence and keep secrets; control yourself in what you say.
evidence_quote: Reticence  is  the  Seal  of  Capacity
rationale: A breast without a secret is an open letter; reticence springs from self-control, and you must pay ransom to each you tell.
argued_against: Having no secrets, like an open letter.

recommendation: Never guide your enemy to what he has to do.
evidence_quote:
Never  guide  the  Enemy  to  what  he  has 
to  do
rationale: The fool never follows the suitable means, and the discreet follow even less a plan laid out by another; attend to what is possible rather than what is probable.
argued_against: Fools who do not follow suitable means.

recommendation: Abide in heedfulness.
evidence_quote:
Do ye abide in
heedfulness.
rationale: All compounded things are subject to decay.

recommendation: Do not weep over parting from those near and dear to you.
evidence_quote:
Enough,
            Ananda! Do not weep!
rationale: It is in the nature of things near and dear that we must separate from them.

recommendation: Be earnest in effort to become free from sensuality, individuality, delusion, and ignorance.
evidence_quote:
Be earnest in
            effort and you too shall be free from the great evils
rationale: Earnest effort brings freedom from the great evils.

recommendation: Give no occasion to reproach yourself.
evidence_quote: Give no occasion to reproach yourself.
rationale: The Mallas might otherwise complain they had no chance to see him in his last hours.
scope: Ananda, in telling the Mallas of the death

recommendation: Tell the Mallas that the Buddha has arrived and will pass away that night.
evidence_quote:
The second thing he told Ananda was to inform
the Mallas of Kushinara that the Blessed One had
arrived there and would pass away in the last watch
of the night.
rationale: So that the Mallas do not reproach themselves for missing his last hours.

recommendation: Correct the public belief that the Buddha died from the food Chunda gave him.
evidence_quote:
He told Ananda to see that belief does not
spread that the Blessed One died as a result of the
food given to Him by Chunda.
rationale: Chunda might otherwise suffer.

recommendation: Know the right time to visit a teacher; this is the mark of a wise man.
evidence_quote:
He knows when it is the right time to come
            and visit the Tathagata
rationale: The Buddha praises Ananda as wise for this.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Treat the remains of the Buddha as men treat the remains of a king of kings.
evidence_quote:
As men treat the remains of a king of kings, so
should you treat the remains of the Tathagata
rationale: none given

recommendation: Keep God in your heart always.
evidence_quote: Have Me, then, in thy heart always! and fight!
rationale: A heart and mind fixed on God leads one to come to him.

recommendation: Meditate on God alone at the hour of death.
evidence_quote:
He that hath meditated Me alone,
  In putting off his flesh, comes forth to Me,
rationale: At death a person goes to what he looked for, because the soul is fashioned to its like.
argued_against: Meditating on anything else at death leads to that other thing.

recommendation: Worship God with never-wavering faith, owning no other gods.
evidence_quote:
All come who cleave
  With never-wavering will of firmest faith,
  Owning none other Gods
rationale: Those who cleave to him this way come to him.

recommendation: At death, shut the senses, lock desire in the heart, fix the breath on the thought of God, and murmur OM.
evidence_quote:
That way--the highest way--goes he who shuts
  The gates of all his senses, locks desire
  Safe in his heart
rationale: This is the highest way to the Ultimate.

recommendation: Look only to God, regarding no other gods.
evidence_quote:
For who, none other Gods regarding, looks
  Ever to Me, easily am I gained
rationale: Such a yogi easily attains God and does not fall back into birth and pain.

recommendation: Receive the royal lore with faith.
evidence_quote:
They that receive not this, failing in faith
  To grasp the greater wisdom, reach not Me
rationale: Those who lack faith in it sink back into the changing realm of flesh.
argued_against: Failing in faith to grasp the greater wisdom.

recommendation: Do not pursue vain hopes, vain deeds, and vain knowledge; worship God as the source of life with unwandering hearts.
evidence_quote:
Vain hopes pursuing, vain deeds doing; fed
  On vainest knowledge, senselessly they seek
  An evil way
rationale: The untaught take the way of brutes and fiends; noble souls who worship God take the celestial path.
argued_against: The untaught who mistake God, veiled in form.

recommendation: Do not seek the fleeting pleasure of heaven through Vedic ritual; seek God.
evidence_quote:
Who seeketh such gaineth the fleeting pleasure
    Of joy which comes and goes!
rationale: Those who earn heaven by rites return to the world of death and change when the reward is spent.
scope: those who follow the threefold scripture for reward
argued_against: Ritual done for the wage of paradise.

recommendation: Offer God a leaf, flower, fruit, or water in faith and love.
evidence_quote:
Whoso shall offer Me in faith and love
  A leaf, a flower, a fruit, water poured forth,
  That offering I accept
rationale: God accepts any offering made lovingly with pious will.

recommendation: Do everything, eating, sacrificing, giving, praying, or fasting, for God and as God's.
evidence_quote:
let it all be done
  For Me, as Mine.
rationale: This frees one from karma, the chain binding men to good and evil results, and brings one to God.

recommendation: Treat morality as the essence of Dhamma; without it there is no Dhamma.
evidence_quote:
Morality is the essence of Dhamma. Without it
there is no Dhamma.
rationale: In Dhamma, morality takes the place of God.

recommendation: Love other people for your own good, not to please God.
evidence_quote:
It is not
to please God that man has to be moral. It is for his
own good that man has to love man.
rationale: Morality arises from the direct need for man to love man and needs no sanction from God.
argued_against: Being moral in order to please God.

recommendation: Do not practice prayers, pilgrimages, rituals, ceremonies, or sacrifices in Dhamma.
evidence_quote:
In Dhamma there is no place for prayers,
pilgrimages, rituals, ceremonies or sacrifices.
rationale: none given
argued_against: Religion centered on God, prayers, rituals, and sacrifices.

recommendation: Make morality sacred and universal, with common rules that are sacred to all.
evidence_quote:
The only way to put a stop to conflict is to have
common rules of morality which are sacred to all.
rationale: Divided groups with different standards produce conflict, inconsistency of mind, and denial of justice.
argued_against: Group-bound morality that protects only group interest.

recommendation: Make fraternity, the brotherhood of men, universally effective.
evidence_quote:
The only remedy lies in
making fraternity universally effective.
rationale: Group set-ups cause discrimination, class stratification, and liberty and equality for only a few.
argued_against: Group rule, stratified classes, and privilege for a few.

recommendation: Do not confine morality to your own group's interest.
evidence_quote:
But this morality is marked by isolation and
            exclusiveness. It is a morality to protect “group interest.”
            It is therefore anti-social.
rationale: Such morality keeps society disorganized and factional, with no common standards, and leads to conflict.
scope: groups such as thieves, businessmen, castes
argued_against: Exclusive group morality, as among thieves, businessmen, castemen, and robber gangs.

recommendation: Do not let empty desire for beauty and women strip away your judgment.
evidence_quote:
into what follies are 
we led by empty desire !
rationale: A man beholding a woman loses power to judge her justly and is consumed with love.
argued_against: Being led by desire into follies.

recommendation: Avoid intimacy with a callet, connection with rogues, and association with bailiffs.
evidence_quote:
connection with a rogue leads to infamy ; and to 
associate with bailiffs will be paid for with your head.
rationale: Such ties bring waste, infamy, and ruin.

recommendation: Do not sport with your prince, with weapons, with fire, or with a strange woman.
evidence_quote:
If you sport with your prince, with weapons, 
with fire, or with a strange woman ; this will lead to 
destruction !
rationale: It leads to destruction.
argued_against: Trifling with dangerous things and people.

recommendation: Reflect that food and women are unprofitable, and relinquish those temptations.
evidence_quote:
He desires pleasant food, and he longs for fair 
women
rationale: Man cannot give them up or reflect for an instant that they are unprofitable.
argued_against: The evil heart that clings to food and women.

recommendation: Judge a person by intrinsic value, not outward appearance; call no one wise who lacks understanding.
evidence_quote:
let no one be called wise who is devoid of un- 
derstanding : his intrinsic, value alone should be considered.
rationale: A buffalo is not lower in price for being black rather than red; value lies within.

recommendation: Do not desert the king even for a thousand others.
evidence_quote: Desert not the king even for a tnousand
rationale: none given

recommendation: Do not tell of food you have given to another, however poor you are.
evidence_quote: when you have given a man food, tell it not
rationale: none given

recommendation: Keep your word.
evidence_quote: The man who cannot keep his word is vile
rationale: One who cannot keep his word is vile, like a pariah.

recommendation: Give food in charity; no charity is superior to bestowing food.
evidence_quote:
no 
charity is superior to that of bestowing food.
rationale: Offering even a little of one's meal to the Lord leads to heaven.

recommendation: Give with kindness, worship with piety, and give gifts with charity.
evidence_quote: A feast given without kindness is a mere waste
rationale: Feasts without kindness, worship without piety, and gifts without charity are wasted.
argued_against: Giving and worship without kindness, piety, and charity.

recommendation: Know yourself before you try to instruct others.
evidence_quote:
Being ignorant of himself, how shall he instruct 
others
rationale: One ignorant of himself cannot instruct others and only performs ceremonies for fees.
argued_against: Idle teachers who perform rites for pitiful fees.

recommendation: Stay true to your own religion, revile no other man's creed, and refrain from evil desire.
evidence_quote:
reviles the creed 
of no other man
rationale: Such a man shall live in happiness and is the first of men.
argued_against: Straying from one's own religion, reviling other creeds, and evil desire.

recommendation: Regard sons, wives, and family ties as unreal and a delusion.
evidence_quote: Sons and wives are a mere delusion
rationale: Pleasure and pain are a deception and the family and affections we feel are unreal.
argued_against: Attachment to family and the delusive life.

recommendation: Look to God, not to family, when you labor for wealth.
evidence_quote:
But if he looked 
to Gods these should no longer exist so as to agitate him .
rationale: Looking to God removes the agitation caused by family attachments.
argued_against: Laboring for wealth for the sake of family.

recommendation: Attend the funeral of a backbiter for decency's sake only; do not pretend to grieve.
evidence_quote: When a backbiter dies, you should go to the
rationale: It is impossible to grieve in reality; a sheep cannot lament the death of the wolf.

recommendation: Avoid covetousness, the worst sin.
evidence_quote: Covetousness is a sin of the worst nature
rationale: Through lust even hermits have been deluded.

recommendation: Do not declare truth to the vile; declare it to a truly great soul.
evidence_quote:
Truth should not be declared to the 
vile
rationale: He who speaks rough plain truth is reproached by all the world.
conditions: Declare truth only to a truly great soul.
argued_against: Speaking plain truth to the vile.

recommendation: Be civil and avoid hypocrisy, baseness, and malice.
evidence_quote: Civility is indispensable in the world
rationale: Hypocrisy is a disgrace, baseness leads to ruin, and malice towards others leads to our own ruin.

recommendation: The elder must rule the younger, and the best of them must rule.
evidence_quote: There can be no doubt that the elder must rule the younger.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Choose as guardians those who show lifelong eagerness to do what is good for their country and revulsion against what harms it.
evidence_quote:
those
who in their whole life show the greatest eagerness to do what is for
the good of their country, and the greatest repugnance to do what is
against her interests.
rationale: A man cares most about what he loves, and loves what he sees as sharing his own interests.

recommendation: Watch the guardians at every age to see that they keep their resolve and never forget their duty to the State.
evidence_quote: they will have to be watched at every age
rationale: A resolution can be lost by theft, force, or enchantment, so it must be tested.

recommendation: Test the youth with toils, pains, terrors, and pleasures, more thoroughly than gold is proved in the furnace.
evidence_quote:
prove them more thoroughly than gold is proved in
the furnace
rationale: To find who is armed against all enchantments and is a good guardian of themselves and of the State.

recommendation: Appoint as ruler and honor greatly the one who comes through every trial victorious and pure; reject the one who fails.
evidence_quote: But him who fails, we must reject.
rationale: none given
conditions: Applies to those tested at every age.

recommendation: Teach citizens that the country is their mother and nurse, and their fellow citizens their brothers, to be defended.
evidence_quote:
they are bound to advise for
her good, and to defend her against attacks, and her citizens they are
to regard as children of the earth and their own brothers.
rationale: The tale says they were formed in the earth, who is their mother.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
conditions: Taught through a deliberate fiction (the royal lie).

recommendation: Rulers should guard above all the purity of the race and watch what elements mingle in their offspring.
evidence_quote:
there is nothing which they should so anxiously guard,
or of which they are to be such good guardians, as of the purity of the
race.
rationale: A god proclaims it as a first principle; an oracle says the State will be destroyed when a man of brass or iron guards it.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not be pitiful to a child of mixed metal; demote them to husbandman or artisan, and raise the gifted to honor.
evidence_quote:
the eye of the
ruler must not be pitiful towards the child
rationale: Nature orders a transposition of ranks when brass or iron mixes in.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
conditions: Applies when a child has an admixture of brass or iron (or of gold or silver).

recommendation: Be thankful to the gods for the good people and circumstances of your life.
evidence_quote:
To the gods I am indebted for having good grandfathers, good
parents, a good sister, good teachers
rationale: The author lists many goods that came through the gods' favor.

recommendation: Begin each morning expecting to meet difficult people, and do not be angry with or hate them.
evidence_quote:
Begin the morning by saying to thyself, I shall meet with the busybody,
the ungrateful, arrogant, deceitful, envious, unsocial.
rationale: They act from ignorance of good and evil; they are akin to me and share in the same intelligence, so they cannot injure me.

recommendation: Cooperate with others; do not act against them by being vexed or turning away.
evidence_quote:
To act against one another,
then, is contrary to nature
rationale: We are made for co-operation, like feet, hands, eyelids, and teeth.
argued_against: Vexation and turning away from others.

recommendation: Throw away your books and stop distracting yourself.
evidence_quote: Throw away thy books; no longer distract thyself
rationale: You are old and near the end; do it as if dying, so you may die cheerfully and thankful.

recommendation: Do not let your ruling part be a puppet pulled by strings, dissatisfied with your lot or afraid of the future.
evidence_quote:
no longer be pulled by the strings like a puppet to unsocial
movements, no longer be either dissatisfied with thy present lot, or
shrink from the future.
rationale: The ruling part is the true self, unlike flesh and breath.
argued_against: Slavery to passion, discontent, and fear.

recommendation: Hold these principles as fixed opinions: the universe is providential and what the whole brings is good for each part.
evidence_quote:
Let these principles be enough for thee; let them
always be fixed opinions.
rationale: All that comes from the gods is full of providence, and what the whole brings is good for every part.

recommendation: Use your limited time to clear the clouds from your mind.
evidence_quote:
a limit of time is fixed for thee, which if thou dost
not use for clearing away the clouds from thy mind, it will go and thou
wilt go, and it will never return.
rationale: Time is limited, you have long put it off, and it will not return.

recommendation: Do every act as if it were your last, with dignity, affection, freedom, and justice, free of carelessness, hypocrisy, self-love, and discontent.
evidence_quote:
doest every act of
thy life as if it were the last
rationale: Few things are needed for a life that flows in quiet, like the existence of the gods.
argued_against: Carelessness, passionate aversion to reason, hypocrisy, self-love, and discontent.

recommendation: Honor yourself and do not place your happiness in the souls of others.
evidence_quote: places thy felicity in the souls of others.
rationale: Your life is nearly finished and you will no longer have the chance to honor yourself.

recommendation: When external things distract you, take time to learn something good, but do not become a trifler with no goal for your activity.
evidence_quote:
Give
thyself time to learn something new and good, and cease to be whirled
around.
rationale: Those who weary themselves with activity but have no object for their thoughts are triflers.

recommendation: Observe the movements of your own mind.
evidence_quote:
those who do not observe the movements of
their own minds must of necessity be unhappy.
rationale: Those who fail to watch their own minds are necessarily unhappy; not watching others' minds seldom causes unhappiness.

recommendation: Always bear in mind the nature of the whole and your place in it, and say and do what accords with that nature.
evidence_quote: This thou must always bear in mind, what is the nature of the whole
rationale: No one hinders you from doing and saying what accords with the nature of which you are part.

recommendation: Treat filial duty as the source of all other virtues and the starting point of education.
evidence_quote:
The duty of children to their
parents is the fountain whence all other virtues spring
rationale: none given
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not injure your body, hair, or skin in the least.
evidence_quote:
we have no right to injure any
of them in the least.
rationale: Body, hair, and skin all derive from our parents.

recommendation: Live uprightly and spread the great doctrines of humanity to win a good name that honors your parents.
evidence_quote:
To live an upright life and to spread the great doctrines of humanity
must win good reputation after death
rationale: A good reputation after death reflects great honor on one's parents.

recommendation: Pay careful attention to every want of your parents, serve your government loyally, and establish a good name.
evidence_quote:
the first duty of a son is to pay a careful attention to every
want of his parents.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Think of your ancestors and keep cultivating the virtue you inherit from them.
evidence_quote:
You must think of your ancestors
and continue to cultivate the virtue which you inherit from them.
rationale: Quoted from a classic text.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Show love and respect to your own parents so that the people follow your example.
evidence_quote:
the Emperor first sets an example to them by showing a dear
love to his mother
rationale: His good conduct influences his people, and his good example will be followed.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not act haughtily, and be frugal and careful in expenses.
evidence_quote:
if he
does not behave himself in a haughty manner
rationale: He stays secure in position and keeps his wealth, and can protect his country and people.

recommendation: Do not wear, say, or do what the good Emperors of old forbade.
evidence_quote:
If we do not put on such dress as our good Emperors of old would
forbid
rationale: Then nobody can find fault with us, and our family avoids serious misfortune and keeps sacrificing to ancestors.

recommendation: Serve your master with the same feelings you have toward your father, and treat venerable persons with respect.
evidence_quote:
If we can serve our August Master with such feelings
as we have toward our father, then loyalty is shown
rationale: Doing so secures a high position and harmony in the circle of one's life.

recommendation: Do nothing in a day that dishonors your ancestors.
evidence_quote:
Do not do anything in the course of a day which will reflect
dishonour upon your ancestors.
rationale: Quoted from a classic text.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Work each season, make land as fertile as possible, and be frugal to keep your parents in comfort.
evidence_quote:
to do the utmost to make lands as
fertile as possible, and to be frugal in their expense
rationale: This is the filial duty of the common people.

recommendation: Do not treat widowers, widows, servants, or the lowly with insolence or haughtiness.
evidence_quote:
dared not treat widowers and
widows with insolence
rationale: It wins the goodwill of subjects and helps in fulfilling filial duty.

recommendation: Love and respect your parents above others.
evidence_quote:
If any one does not love his
parents, but others, he is a rebel against virtue
rationale: Natural affection grows into reverence, and we receive boundless kindness from our parents.
argued_against: Loving and respecting others instead of one's parents.

recommendation: Gain high position by good actions, not by undue influence.
evidence_quote:
any one who gets
a high position, such as that of a ruler, by undue influence instead
of by good actions, will be despised by good men.
rationale: Such persons will be despised by good men.
argued_against: Gaining high position by undue influence.

recommendation: Do not let young people hear tales of gods quarreling, plotting, and fighting; teach that quarreling is unholy.
evidence_quote:
these tales must not be admitted into
our State
rationale: The young cannot judge allegory from literal truth, and what they first take in becomes indelible.
scope: the young in the ideal state
argued_against: Tales of battles and quarrels of gods and heroes.

recommendation: Make the first tales the young hear models of virtuous thoughts.
evidence_quote:
it is most important
that the tales which the young first hear should be models of virtuous
thoughts.
rationale: Whatever a young person receives into the mind is likely to become indelible and unalterable.

recommendation: Always represent God as he truly is: good.
evidence_quote:
God is always to be represented as
he truly is
rationale: God is good, the good does no harm, and so God causes only good.
scope: all poets and tellers of tales

recommendation: Do not say that God, being good, causes evil; deny it strenuously and do not sing or hear it.
evidence_quote:
that God being good is the author of evil to any one is to be
strenuously denied
rationale: Such a fiction is suicidal, ruinous, and impious; the causes of evils are to be sought elsewhere than in God.
scope: young and old in a well-ordered commonwealth
argued_against: Poets like Homer who say Zeus dispenses good and evil, or that God plants guilt in men.

recommendation: If a poet says the punished suffered, he must say they were benefited and that God acted justly.
evidence_quote:
he must
say that God did what was just and right, and they were the better for
being punished
rationale: The wicked are miserable because they require punishment, and are benefited by receiving it from God.
argued_against: Saying God is the author of the misery of the punished.

recommendation: Do not say that gods change shape or walk about disguised as strangers.
evidence_quote: let none of the poets tell us that
rationale: God is perfect, cannot be compelled to change, and would not change himself for the worse, so he remains forever in his own form.
argued_against: Poets who slander Proteus and Thetis or show Here disguised as a priestess.

recommendation: Do not let mothers scare their children with bad versions of myths about gods in disguise.
evidence_quote:
Neither must we have mothers
under the influence of the poets scaring their children
rationale: Such tales make cowards of children and blaspheme the gods.
argued_against: Mothers frightening children with myths of gods roaming in disguise.

recommendation: Live only in the present, which is your real life, and you will pass the rest of your life free from perturbations.
evidence_quote:
strive to live only what is really thy life, that is,
the present
rationale: Living only the present lets you spend the remaining life free from disturbance, nobly, and obedient to your inner god.

recommendation: Practise even the things you despair of accomplishing.
evidence_quote:
Practise thyself even in the things which thou despairest of
accomplishing.
rationale: The left hand, useless for other tasks, holds the bridle better than the right because it has been practised at it.

recommendation: Consider the shortness of life and the boundless abyss of time past and future.
evidence_quote:
consider the shortness of life, the
boundless abyss of time past and future, the feebleness of all matter
rationale: none given

recommendation: Apply your principles like the pancratiast, who always has his hand ready, not like the gladiator, who drops his sword.
evidence_quote:
In the application of thy principles thou must be like the
pancratiast, not like the gladiator
rationale: The gladiator drops his sword and is killed; the pancratiast always has his hand and only needs to use it.

recommendation: Blame nobody for what happens in accord with nature.
evidence_quote: we should blame nobody
rationale: The gods do nothing wrong, and men do wrong only involuntarily.
conditions: Applies to what happens conformably to nature.

recommendation: Do not resist necessity; if providence exists make yourself worthy of divine help; if there is chaos be content with your ruling intelligence.
evidence_quote:
If then there is an invincible necessity, why dost thou
resist?
rationale: Whichever of the three cases holds, your own intelligence cannot be carried away by the tempest.
conditions: Depends on whether the world is necessity, providence, or confusion.

recommendation: If it is not right, do not do it; if it is not true, do not say it.
evidence_quote: If it is not right, do not do it: if it is not true, do not say it.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Do nothing inconsiderately or without a purpose, and make your acts serve a social end.
evidence_quote: make thy acts refer to nothing else than to a social end
rationale: none given

recommendation: Remember that everything is opinion and opinion is in your power; remove your opinion and find calm.
evidence_quote: Consider that everything is opinion, and opinion is in thy power.
rationale: Removing your opinion brings calm, like a mariner who has passed a promontory and finds a waveless bay.

recommendation: Do not be irritable at wrongdoers; expect wrongdoing as you expect figs to have juice, and cure your own irritable disposition.
evidence_quote:
If then thou art irritable, + cure this man's
disposition.
rationale: You cannot know the act is wrong or that the doer has not condemned himself; wrongdoing is as necessary as a horse neighing.
argued_against: wanting bad people not to do wrong

recommendation: Do not be surprised at anything that happens in life.
evidence_quote:
How ridiculous and what a stranger he is who is surprised at
anything which happens in life.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Perceive that you have within you something more divine than the passions that pull you like strings, such as fear, suspicion, or desire.
evidence_quote:
Perceive at last that thou hast in thee something better and more
divine than the things which cause the various affects
rationale: none given
argued_against: being pulled by fear, suspicion, desire

recommendation: Do not be proud of human things; they show only sameness of form and shortness of duration.
evidence_quote: Are these things to be proud of?
rationale: Seen from above, human affairs always show the same forms and brief duration.

recommendation: Consider that before long you will be nobody and nowhere, since all things are formed by nature to change and perish.
evidence_quote: Consider that before long thou wilt be nobody and nowhere
rationale: All things are formed by nature to change and perish so that other things may succeed.

recommendation: Do not dispute with the gods about the order of things, such as the extinction of the dead.
evidence_quote:
we should not
thus dispute with the gods
rationale: Disputing with the gods is unfitting because they are most excellent and just and would not neglect anything unjustly.

recommendation: Do not let the truth, justice, and temperance in you be extinguished before your death.
evidence_quote:
shall the truth which is in thee and justice and
temperance be extinguished [before thy death]?
rationale: A lamp shines with undimmed splendor until it is extinguished.

recommendation: Regard the end of life as no evil, since it comes at its proper time and is in harmony with the whole.
evidence_quote:
the
termination of life for every man is no evil
rationale: An activity that ceases at its proper time suffers no evil; nature fixes the limit, and what is useful to the universe is good and in season.

recommendation: Do not value your own opinion of yourself less than other people's opinion of you.
evidence_quote:
So much more respect have
we to what our neighbors shall think of us than to what we shall think
of ourselves.
rationale: Men love themselves most yet fear their neighbors' view more than their own; they could not bear to voice every thought.
argued_against: deferring to others' opinion over one's own

recommendation: Rulers, like true physicians and pilots, should consider the interest of their subjects, not their own.
evidence_quote:
there is no one in any rule who, in so far
as he is a ruler, considers or enjoins what is for his own interest,
but always what is for the interest of his subject
rationale: Every true art cares only for the interest of its subject, not itself or the stronger; the physician heals and the pilot serves the sailors.
conditions: Applies to a ruler in the strict sense, in so far as he is a ruler.
argued_against: the claim that justice is the interest of the stronger

recommendation: Inquire seriously into how life may be passed by each person to the greatest advantage.
evidence_quote:
Is the attempt to
determine the way of man’s life so small a matter in your eyes
rationale: none given
argued_against: treating the question of how to live as a small matter

recommendation: Be beneficent by relieving the poor and miserable, not by giving to the rich for applause.
evidence_quote:
He alone can be called beneficent who relieves the 
poor and miserable
rationale: Giving merely to the rich is liberality only for the sake of applause.
argued_against: giving to the rich for applause

recommendation: Do not give presents to the rich; they are useless.
evidence_quote:
equally useless are presents made to the 
rich
rationale: Like food thrown away by one with weak digestion, gifts to the rich are unprofitable.

recommendation: Subdue your heart in order to attain release.
evidence_quote:
unless thou subdue 
thy heart, how shalt thou attain release
rationale: A man who gives rein to lust all his life and turns recluse only at death cannot attain release.
argued_against: indulging lusts then turning recluse at death

recommendation: Value eminence as depending on virtue, not on birth.
evidence_quote:
Eminence depends 
not upon birth, but virtue.
rationale: Cited example: a savage became a Brahmin by devoutly repeating a sacred name.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Use wealth you acquire with liberality.
evidence_quote:
If after acquiring wealth he use it not with 
liberality
rationale: Like the bee that stores honey and leaves it to others, a miser cannot keep what he hoards.

recommendation: Be wise, attain the deity, and be forever happy.
evidence_quote:
be wise? attain 
it, a nd be for ever happy !
rationale: The deity is evident and manifest.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Restrain your heart and direct it to the Lord of all.
evidence_quote:
He who duly restrains his heart, and directs it to 
the Lord of all, is the noblest of his tribe
rationale: Without this one cannot attain happiness.

recommendation: Keep your mind firmly on the deity and never let your heart swerve from him.
evidence_quote:
If thou stay thy mind firmly on the deity, beati- 
tude shall be thine
rationale: Firm devotion brings beatitude; even slight swerving forfeits heaven.

recommendation: Beware of three sins: disobedience to your mother, rebellion against your father, and despising your elder brother.
evidence_quote:
Conduct -thyself so as to beware of three sins — 
•disobedience to thy mother, rebellion against thy father, 
and despising thy elder brother.
rationale: none given
argued_against: disobeying parents and despising elder brother

recommendation: Avoid avarice and lust; they can ruin any dominion.
evidence_quote:
Avarice and lust are sufficient to rain any 
dominion
rationale: Human plans fail and perish; the thoughts of men are one way and God's providence another.

recommendation: Give food to the hungry; this is as meritorious as a sacrifice.
evidence_quote:
To give food to the hungry is as meritorious as- 
offering it in sacrifice
rationale: Charity to the poor is as meritorious as sacrifice, and liberality leads to wealth.

recommendation: Give charity and be beneficent, since liberality and beneficence lead to wealth.
evidence_quote:
As surely as figures added to figures form a total, 
iso surely shall liberality and beneficence lead to wealth.
rationale: Liberality leads to wealth as surely as added figures form a total.

recommendation: Give alms; those who have and give nothing will receive nothing in the next birth.
evidence_quote:
Those who have and bestow not (0 ye poor !) 
shall in their next birth not receive even alms.
rationale: Alms given return to the giver; he who bestows nothing receives nothing.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not grieve over lacking the wealth you see in others' houses.
evidence_quote:
Why should a man grieve because he lacks the 
■wealth which he sees heaped up in the houses of others ?
rationale: Their wealth is the fruit of past charity; the grieving man died in a former birth without any charitable act.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: A mendicant should give alms from what he has received; this makes begging honorable.
evidence_quote:
If a mendicant bestows as alms any part of what 
he has received in charity, this renders his begging not dis- 
graceful, but honourable.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Do not treat possessions as your own; what you have given to others alone is yours.
evidence_quote:
That alone is yours which 
you have bestowed on others
rationale: Only fools agree you own what you keep; the rest is not at your disposal.

recommendation: Do not hoard wealth for your sons or bury it; use it yourself or give it in charity.
evidence_quote:
If thou consume it not thyself, nor bestow it in 
charity, but hoard up thy wealth for thy sons
rationale: Hoarded wealth falls to strangers; buried wealth gives no benefit and only causes anxiety.

recommendation: Injure not others, and be careful to escape the pains of hell.
evidence_quote:
injure not 
others, O men, and live for ever !
rationale: Avoiding injury to others saves one from the pains of hell and brings eternal life.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not make promises you cannot keep or put off payment with false words.
evidence_quote:
He who, without considering his own means, 
.makes oral promises and deludes you
rationale: The one who deludes with promises will suddenly perish.
argued_against: promising beyond one's means and deluding others

recommendation: Do not rely on fortune-telling, possession by demons, dreams, auguries, or divination.
evidence_quote:
Fortune-tellingj possession />y 0 demons dreams- 
of sleep, idle wishes, and pleasing auguries, with divina- 
tions of all sorts, * turn out true or false, as it may happen
rationale: They turn out true or false by chance, so none can rely on them.

recommendation: Call the divinity your helper; he will surely aid you.
evidence_quote:
if thou call him thy helper,, 
he will surely aid thee
rationale: Denying the deity makes him inaccessible and of no avail to you.

recommendation: Value having a son and growing old together as the greatest blessings of marriage, above riches.
evidence_quote:
Surely the possession of a son is the first of 
blessings, and to grow old together is the greatest of all 
riches.
rationale: none given
argued_against: treating riches as the real wealth of marriage

recommendation: Give up your identification with egoism immediately.
evidence_quote:
Give  up  immediately  thy  identi- 
fication with  the  Egoism
rationale: Identifying with egoism, a modification, diverts one from the Self and brings the miseries of birth, decay, and death.

recommendation: Destroy egoism, your enemy, with the great sword of realisation and enjoy the bliss of your own empire.
evidence_quote:
destroying  this  Egoism, 
thy  enemy
rationale: Egoism is like a thorn in the throat; destroying it gives the bliss of the Self.

recommendation: Check the activities of egoism, give up all attachment, and remain quiet in Brahman, free from duality.
evidence_quote:
checking  the  activities 
of  Egoism  etc.,  and  giving  np  all  attach- 
uient
rationale: Through realising the Supreme Reality you have attained your infinite nature.

recommendation: Do not give egoism even a moment's respite by thinking on sense-objects.
evidence_quote:
not  a  moment's  respite  should  b&  given  to 
it  by  thinking  on  sense-objects
rationale: Thinking on sense-objects revives egoism, like water reviving a nearly dried citron tree; even a rooted-out egoism returns if brooded over for a moment.

recommendation: Subdue the effects, meaning selfish actions, since the seed of desire is destroyed when effects are destroyed.
evidence_quote:
Therefore  one  must 
subdue  the  effects.
rationale: Seed and effects rise and fall together; desires increase selfish work and selfish work increases desire, so transmigration never ends.

recommendation: The Sannyasin should burn to ashes both the thinking of sense-objects and selfish acts, to break the chain of transmigration.
evidence_quote:
the  Sannvasin  should 
burn  to  ashes  those  two
rationale: Thinking of sense-objects and doing selfish acts increase desires and so keep one in transmigration.

recommendation: Look upon everything, always and everywhere, as Brahman alone, and strengthen the longing to be one with Brahman.
evidence_quote:
looking  upon  everything,  under  all  cir- 
cumstances, always,  everywhere  and  in  all 
respects,  as  Brahman  and  Brahman  alone
rationale: This destroys desire, selfish action, and brooding on sense-objects.

recommendation: Meditate on the Reality watchfully while any residue of past action remains.
evidence_quote:
one  should  pass  one's  time 
watchfully
rationale: none given
conditions: Applies if there is any residue of Prarabdha work left.

recommendation: Never be careless in your steadfastness to Brahman.
evidence_quote:
One  should  never  be  careless  in 
one's  steadfastness  to  Brahman.
rationale: Inadvertence is death itself; from it come delusion, egoism, bondage, and misery.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Carefully concentrate your mind on Brahman.
evidence_quote:
carefully  concentrate  thy  mind  (on  Brah- 
man)
rationale: The concentrated man attains complete success; inadvertence is the worst death.

recommendation: Give up reflecting on sense-objects, the root of all mischief.
evidence_quote:
one  shoujd  give  up  re- 
flecting on  sense-objects
rationale: Reflection on sense-objects leads from attachment to desire and action, and causes the bondage of transmigration.

recommendation: Do not identify yourself with the objective universe.
evidence_quote:
He  who  identifies  himself  with  the 
objective  universe
rationale: Such a person experiences misery after misery, like a thief doing something forbidden; those who dwell on the unreal are destroyed.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: The Sannyasin should give up dwelling on the unreal and always fix his thoughts on the Atman as 'I myself am This.'
evidence_quote:
The  Sannyasin  should  give  up 
dwelling  on  the  unreal
rationale: Steadfastness in Brahman through realising one's identity with It gives bliss and removes the misery born of Nescience.

recommendation: Avoid external objects and constantly apply yourself to meditation on the Atman.
evidence_quote:
one  should  avoid  the  external  ob- 
jects and  constantly  apply  oneself  to  medi- 
tation on  the  Atman
rationale: Dwelling on external objects intensifies evil propensities that grow worse; shutting out the external world makes the mind cheerful and leads to Liberation.

recommendation: Do not boast of purity, learning, or twice-born status or scorn others; the humble palmer is better than such boasters.
evidence_quote:
Truly the poorest palmer is better 
than such boasters.
rationale: Those who are born Sudras, revile Sudras, or scorn Parias while lacking good qualities are the lowest; the title does not make them twice-born.
argued_against: boasting of caste, purity, or scripture learning while scorning others

recommendation: Do not lie; falsehood is the greatest sin.
evidence_quote: There is no sin greater than that of falsehood
rationale: none given
argued_against: falsehood, including claiming to be twice-born falsely

recommendation: Be pure within; outward garb, ashes, shaved heads, and ornaments do not make a saint.
evidence_quote:
No man is a 
• saint who is not p ure within.
rationale: Ashes will not remove the smell of a winepot; an ass can wallow in dirt as well.
argued_against: relying on religious garb, ashes, and outward marks

recommendation: Set your thoughts on God alone.
evidence_quote:
your thoughts should be set on God 
-alone
rationale: none given
argued_against: smearing with ashes without inner devotion

recommendation: Do not rely on postures, breath exercises, or austere penance; they are mere learned tricks.
evidence_quote:
The religious postures, 
are mere tricks that are learnt.
rationale: Austerities do not gain heaven; ascetics vex their bodies because they are ignorant of the truth.
argued_against: ascetic postures, penance, leaving home, breath control

recommendation: Do not boast of mere oral divinity or of breath control when you lack inward vision.
evidence_quote:
In the absence of inward vision boast not of mere oral 
divinity.
rationale: none given
argued_against: haughty monks who think breath gestures bring wisdom

recommendation: Cease bowing to stone images; the deity does not dwell in stone.
evidence_quote:
cease from 
these ideas
rationale: There is nothing in a stone; the true temple is the body and the god is the soul within.

recommendation: Recognize the deity within yourself; the body is the true temple.
evidence_quote:
The true 
temple is the body, the soul is the god therein
rationale: The stone in a temple does not change its nature; those who adore the living principle should not honor images.

recommendation: Forsake tribe and caste when you embrace a creed.
evidence_quote:
It is good to forsake tribe and caste and become 
a hermit
rationale: Instruction is of no good while you retain caste; in the Zangam sect former caste is forgotten like the names of woods in a ship.

recommendation: Learn the greatness of God and you will live; hearing the Vedas and Sastras is of no use.
evidence_quote:
Learn the greatness of God, and verily you 
•shall live.
rationale: Listening to the Vedas and Sastras leaves you roaming from house to house until you die.
argued_against: relying on the Vedas, Sastras, and numerous rites

recommendation: Give to good men rather than feeding crows in the name of ancestors.
evidence_quote: give rather to good men ?
rationale: A dung-eating crow cannot be your ancestor, so charity to crows has no good.

recommendation: Do not abstain from the present life; eternal existence begins in this life.
evidence_quote:
False is the creed of those who hold that it is profit- 
able to renounce the present life
rationale: Eternal existence commences in this life.

recommendation: Believe that you are the agent of your own conduct and will be rewarded or punished accordingly.
evidence_quote:
what we gain is the result not of fate but ou r own 
conduct
rationale: The deity bestows only what is destined, but we are agents of all we do.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Regard the heart as the only basis of salvation, not ordination or religious exercises.
evidence_quote: the heart is the only basis of salvation
rationale: If the heart is set aright, formal ordination as a monk is of no use.
argued_against: reliance on regular ordination and ritual

recommendation: Do not follow the practices of the Embari sect, such as eating flesh and drinking wine.
evidence_quote:
Those who embrace the Embari f sect eat flesh, 
change their names and drink wine
rationale: They transgress the lines of consanguinity and become the portion of the grave.

recommendation: Worship the compassionate Lord Hari and cease from all wrangling and hypocrisy.
evidence_quote:
Worship  him,  says  poor  [PERSON]  DAs,   and  cease 
from  all  wrangling  and  hypocrisy.
rationale: Hari is compassionate beyond our deserts, as shown by the redemption of the cursed woman.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Serve God with fullest service, perfect faith, and uttermost surrender; no Vedas, sacrifice, penance, or gifts alone reveal him.
evidence_quote:
Only by fullest service, perfect faith,
  And uttermost surrender am I known
rationale: The vision cannot be gained by Vedas, sacrifice, penance, gift-giving, or prayer.
argued_against: relying on Vedas, sacrifice, penance, or gifts alone

recommendation: Do all for God, find him in all, adore always, and love all that he has made.
evidence_quote:
Who doeth all for Me; who findeth Me
  In all; adoreth always; loveth all
rationale: Such a man comes to God.

recommendation: Worship God as revealed, constantly true and fixed in devotion; this is holier than the hard path of the Unmanifest.
evidence_quote:
Whoever serve Me--as I show Myself--
  Constantly true, in full devotion fixed,
  Those hold I very holy.
rationale: The path to the Unmanifest is hard for those bearing the flesh.
argued_against: the hard path of worshipping the Unmanifest

recommendation: Do all your deeds renouncing self for God, and keep your mind on him night and day.
evidence_quote:
whereso any doeth all his deeds
  Renouncing self for Me, full of Me
rationale: God will swiftly lift him from life's ocean of distress and death.

recommendation: Cling to God and clasp him with heart and mind.
evidence_quote:
Cling thou to Me!
  Clasp Me with heart and mind!
rationale: Thus you shall dwell surely with God on high.

recommendation: If you cannot fix your mind on God, do not despair; offer lower service, steadfast worship, or works pleasing to him.
evidence_quote: Despair not! give Me lower service!
rationale: He who labors right for love of God shall finally attain.
conditions: Applies if you are too weak to set body and soul on God constantly; fall back from steadfast worship to works.

recommendation: If even that fails, give up the fruits of your labor, renouncing hope, with a lowly heart, and take refuge in God.
evidence_quote:
let fruits of labour go,
  Renouncing hope for Me, with lowliest heart
rationale: Renunciation is better than knowing or worship, and near it dwells Eternal Peace.
conditions: Applies if the faint heart fails at the lower service.

recommendation: Value worship above knowing, and renunciation above worship.
evidence_quote:
worship better is
  Than knowing, and renouncing better still.
rationale: Near to renunciation dwells Eternal Peace.

recommendation: Hate nothing that lives; be benign, compassionate, free of arrogance and self-love, patient, contented, and true to your word.
evidence_quote:
Who hateth nought
  Of all which lives, living himself benign,
  Compassionate, from arrogance exempt
rationale: God loves the man who has these qualities.

recommendation: Keep an equal heart to friend and foe, praise and blame, pleasure and pain, and be unmoved by good or ill fortune.
evidence_quote:
Who, unto friend and foe
  Keeping an equal heart, with equal mind
  Bears shame and glory
rationale: God loves such a man.
argued_against: being swayed by praise, blame, pleasure, pain, desire

recommendation: Do not trouble others or be troubled by them; be free of wrath, and live above gladness, grief, and fear.
evidence_quote:
Who troubleth not his kind,
  And is not troubled by them; clear of wrath
rationale: God loves such a man.

recommendation: Work for God yet stay detached from the results of all works.
evidence_quote: Working with Me, yet from all works detached
rationale: God loves such a man.

recommendation: Cultivate humbleness, truthfulness, harmlessness, patience, self-control, and detachment from home, wife, and children; love solitude and shun the noise of foolish crowds.
evidence_quote:
Humbleness, truthfulness, and harmlessness,
  Patience and honour, reverence for the wise.
rationale: These qualities are true Wisdom; whatever is otherwise is ignorance.
argued_against: attachment to home and family, crowds, sense-delights

recommendation: See the one living Soul in all alike, in every form.
evidence_quote:
He sees indeed who sees in all alike
  The living, lordly Soul
rationale: Whoever beholds this does no wrongfulness to himself and goes the highest road to bliss.

recommendation: Practise penance; it is the means of approach to Siva, and there is no other way of escaping sorrow.
evidence_quote:
Penance  is  the  means  of  approach  to  Siva, 
and  there  is  no  other  way  of  escaping  sorrow.
rationale: Penance is full of peace and ends pain and sin; creation, preservation, and destruction all depend on it, and Siva is quickly satisfied by it.

recommendation: Do not presume to copy the powerful, saying it is the same for a man as for a god.
evidence_quote:
The  fool  who  in  the  pride  of  knowledge  presumes  to  copy 
them
rationale: Saints will not drink wine though made with Ganges water, while the Ganges stays pure; the fool who copies them is cast into hell.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: the fool who copies gods or the powerful from pride in knowledge

recommendation: Put away anxiety and fix your thoughts on the good God who created and will protect your child.
evidence_quote:
Put  away  all  anxiety,  my  dear,  and  fix  your  thoughts 
on  the  good  God
rationale: God, who created Parvati, will protect her.

recommendation: Recognize the truth about Siva and doubt not.
evidence_quote:
recognize  this  truth  and 
doubt  not
rationale: Narad's words are pregnant with meaning and Mahadeva is beautiful, accomplished, and irreproachable.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Submit to the commands of God and cease to resist when your father comes to call you.
evidence_quote: submit  now  to  my  commands
rationale: The commands are ever true and ever good.

recommendation: Pray for discretion as the first and best quality.
evidence_quote:
should 
be  prayed  for  as  the  first  and  best  quality
rationale: It is the throne of reason and foundation of prudence; it brings success cheaply; all actions depend on it; without it a man is imperfect.

recommendation: Obtain and preserve a reputation.
evidence_quote: Obtain  and  preserve  a  Reputation.
rationale: Reputation confers obligations and, if based on elevated powers, brings veneration and majesty; once obtained it is easily preserved.
conditions: Obtaining it is costly because it attaches only to rare distinguished abilities; only a well-founded reputation lasts.

recommendation: Disguise your passions and intentions; adopt the policy of the cuttlefish.
evidence_quote: Write  your  Intentions  in  Cypher
rationale: Passions are the gates of the soul; hiding them is the most practical knowledge; exposed cards risk losing the stakes; caution must combat inquirers' curiosity.
argued_against: Playing with cards exposed; revealing one's passions

recommendation: Do not let even your tastes be known.
evidence_quote: Do  not  even  let  your  tastes  be  known
rationale: Others may use known tastes against you, by running counter to them or flattering them.

recommendation: Make sure that being right also looks right.
evidence_quote:
It  is  not  enough  to  be  right,  if  right 
seem  false  and  ill.
rationale: Things pass for what they seem, not what they are; few see inside and many take to the outside.
argued_against: Relying on being right without regard to how it appears

recommendation: Be truly a man without illusions, a wise Christian, and a philosophic courtier, not merely seem or pretend to be.
evidence_quote: Be  all  these,  not  merely  seem  to  be  them
rationale: Philosophy was always the chief concern of the wise, even if now discredited.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: Merely seeming or pretending to be wise or philosophic

recommendation: Value the discovery of deceit as nourishment for a thoughtful mind.
evidence_quote:
the  discovery  of  deceit 
was  always  thought  the  true  nourishment  of  a 
thoughtful  mind
rationale: It has always been thought the true delight of a virtuous soul.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
argued_against: Discrediting philosophy and the art of thinking

recommendation: Aim to be independent of any one vote, fashion, or century.
evidence_quote:
You  should  aim  to 
be  independent  of  any  one  vote,  of  any  one 
fashion,  of  any  one  century.
rationale: Tastes differ widely; what one pursues another persecutes; every defect finds admirers and every excellence finds critics.
argued_against: Letting a single opinion or fashion decide worth

recommendation: Treat the approval of famous men and experts as the real test of praise.
evidence_quote:
The  real  test 
of  praise  is  the  approbation  of  famous  men  and 
of  experts  in  the  matter.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Do not lose heart when some are displeased, and do not let applause turn your head.
evidence_quote:
Nor  need 
their  applause  turn  our  head
rationale: Others will appreciate what some dislike, and others will condemn what some applaud.

recommendation: Do not try to regulate everything by your own ideas.
evidence_quote:
ass  that  would  regulate  everything 
according  to  his  ideas.
rationale: Excellences do not depend on one man's pleasure; so many men, so many tastes.
argued_against: The man who regulates everything by his own ideas

recommendation: A man of talent should show he has room for greater enterprises and avoid showing signs of a little heart.
evidence_quote:
above  all  avoid  showing  signs  of  a 
little  heart.
rationale: Those without capacity for great luck are turned by undeserved honors and risk much in high place; big luck does not embarrass one who can digest bigger.
argued_against: Having a small capacity for luck and honors

recommendation: Make each deed princely within your station, in all things like a king in merit if not might.
evidence_quote:
Let  each  deed  of  a  man  in  its  degree,  though 
he  be  not  a  king,  be  worthy  of  a  prince
rationale: True kingship lies in spotless rectitude; one who can be a model of greatness need not envy it.
conditions: Within due limits of one's station

recommendation: Those near the throne should prefer sharing the true qualities of royalty to its mere ceremonies.
evidence_quote:
prefer  to 
share  the  true  qualities  of  royalty  rather  than 
take  parts  in  its  mere  ceremonies
rationale: none given
argued_against: Taking part in mere ceremonies; copying royal imperfections

recommendation: Prefer offices that leave you free, combine variety with importance, and depend little on others.
evidence_quote:
Those  are  better  that  leave  a  man 
free  to  follow  his  own  devices,  combining 
variety  with  importance
rationale: Change refreshes the mind; offices with fixed hours and routine are intolerable; those with least dependence on others are most in repute.
argued_against: Offices with fixed hours and settled routine; offices that worry us both here and hereafter

recommendation: Avoid being a bore; be brief.
evidence_quote:
avoid 
being  bores
rationale: Brevity flatters and does better business; good things are twice as good when short; talkative folk rarely have sense; boring the great is worst.
argued_against: The man of one business or one topic; talkative folk

recommendation: Do not parade your position.
evidence_quote: Do  not  parade  your  Position.
rationale: Outshining in dignity is offensive; posing as a personage earns hatred; esteem cannot be taken, only earned from others.
argued_against: Posing as a personage; insisting on the dignity of one's office

recommendation: Do not enforce respect; create it, while keeping enough dignity to carry out the duties of the office.
evidence_quote:
Do  not 
enforce  respect,  but  try  and  create  it.
rationale: Great positions need enough authority to be efficient; those who insist on office dignity show they have not deserved it.
conditions: Preserve enough dignity to carry on the duties of the office
argued_against: Insisting on the dignity of one's office

recommendation: If you wish to be valued, be valued for your talents, not for anything adventitious.
evidence_quote:
If  you  wish  to  be  valued, 
be  valued  for  your  talents,  not  for  anything 
adventitious.
rationale: Even kings prefer to be honored for personal qualifications rather than station.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Show no self-satisfaction; be neither discontented with yourself nor self-satisfied, and keep a healthy distrust.
evidence_quote: Show  no  Self-satisfaction.
rationale: Self-satisfaction is folly arising from ignorance and injures credit; distrust helps evade mishaps and console us, since a feared misfortune cannot surprise.
conditions: Being discontented with oneself is also wrong, as poor-spirited

recommendation: Choose friends of contrasting temperaments so that joining extremes yields the golden mean.
evidence_quote:
by  joining  extremes  the  more  effective  middle 
way  is  found
rationale: Intercourse shares manners and taste and grows good sense and talent; the alternation of contraries sustains the world.

recommendation: The seeker after liberation must first strengthen discrimination and renunciation.
evidence_quote:
the  wise  seeker  after  Liberation 
must  first  strengthen  these  two.
rationale: Through the preponderance of discrimination and renunciation the mind attains purity and makes for liberation.

recommendation: Good people who long for liberation must never go into the forest of sense pleasures, where the mind prowls like a tiger.
evidence_quote: never  go  there
rationale: The mind is likened to a huge tiger prowling in the forest-tract of sense pleasures.

recommendation: The seeker after liberation must carefully purify the mind.
evidence_quote: must  carefully  purify  the  mind.
