rationale: The mind alone causes bondage or liberation; when purified, liberation is as easy as a fruit in the palm.
argued_against: A mind tainted by Rajas and Tamas

recommendation: Root out attachment to sense-objects, renounce selfish actions, and regularly practice hearing, reflection, and meditation with faith in Brahman.
evidence_quote:
regularly  practises  hearing  etc., 
succeeds  in  purging  the  Rajasic  nature  of 
the  intellect
rationale: This course, followed with one-pointed devotion to liberation, purges the passionate nature of the intellect.
conditions: Actions renounced are those done with selfish motives

recommendation: Do not identify the Self with the mind or knowledge sheath; the subject is never the object of knowledge.
evidence_quote:
Whereas  the  subject  can 
never  be  identified  with  the  objects  of 
knowledge.
rationale: The mental sheath has a beginning and end, is subject to change and pain, and is an object, so it cannot be the Supreme Self.
argued_against: Mistaking the body, organs, and mind for the Self

recommendation: The first thing to attend to is the culture of the mind.
evidence_quote:
The first thing to attend to is the culture of
            the mind.
rationale: Mind precedes, dominates, and creates things; it leads all faculties and is the source of all good and evil.

recommendation: Clean the mind; this is the essence of religion.
evidence_quote:
The cleaning
of the mind is, therefore, the essence of religion.
rationale: Affliction follows one who speaks or acts with a flawed mind as cart wheels follow the bullocks' feet.
argued_against: Speaking or acting with a corrupted mind

recommendation: Avoid all sinful acts.
evidence_quote: the avoidance of all sinful acts
rationale: none given

recommendation: Real religion lies in observing its tenets, not in religious books.
evidence_quote:
real religion lies not in the books of religion but
in the observance of the tenets of the religion
rationale: none given
argued_against: Treating religious books as religion itself

recommendation: Do not escape from the world; change the world and make it better.
evidence_quote:
What is
            necessary is to change the world and to make it better.
rationale: There is no escape from the world, even for an ascetic; the world has much unhappiness and conflict, and sitting idle as a recluse is wrong.
argued_against: Withdrawal from the world as a sanyasi; asceticism

recommendation: Do not engage in asceticism or the uprooting of natural instincts and desires.
evidence_quote: Asceticism he found to be useless.
rationale: Escape from the world is impossible, and asceticism subjects life to complete subjugation of instincts and desires.

recommendation: Do not indulge in speculation about whence, whither, and what am I.
evidence_quote:
He condemned indulging in speculation as to the
         whence, whither and what am I
rationale: none given
argued_against: Speculation about origins, destiny, and self

recommendation: Reject fatalism, including predestination by a God and the view that past deeds make present activity impotent.
evidence_quote: He repudiated the fatalistic view of life
rationale: Fatalism is foolish, makes man a slave of destiny so he cannot liberate himself, and renders present activity impotent.
argued_against: Fatalistic views of life and Karma

recommendation: Accept the law of cause and effect.
evidence_quote:
He accepted the great grand law of cause and
                      effect with its corollaries.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Put righteousness above selfishness.
evidence_quote:
my doctrine of righteousness overriding
     selfishness
rationale: Mankind is intent on its selfishness and finds it hard to accept this doctrine.

recommendation: A superior man takes office and performs the righteous duties belonging to it.
evidence_quote:
A superior man takes office, and performs the righteous duties
belonging to it.
rationale: The sovereign-minister relation is a great duty; withdrawing to keep personal purity throws it into confusion.
conditions: He knows that right principles may fail to make progress
argued_against: Withdrawing from office to maintain personal purity

recommendation: Have no course predetermined for or against; stay flexible.
evidence_quote:
I have no course for which I
am predetermined, and no course against which I am
predetermined.
rationale: none given
argued_against: Rigid fixed courses, as with the recluses described

recommendation: A virtuous prince does not neglect his relations.
evidence_quote: The virtuous prince does not neglect his relations.
rationale: none given

recommendation: A prince should not make his great ministers resent that he does not employ them.
evidence_quote:
He does
not cause the great ministers to repine at his not employing them.
rationale: none given

recommendation: Do not dismiss members of old families from office without some great cause.
evidence_quote:
Without some great cause, he does not dismiss from their offices
the members of old families.
rationale: none given
conditions: Unless there is some great cause

recommendation: Do not look for talents for every employment in one man.
evidence_quote:
He does not seek in one man talents
for every employment.
rationale: none given
argued_against: Demanding all talents of one man

recommendation: In threatening danger, be prepared to sacrifice your life.
evidence_quote: seeing threatening danger, is prepared to sacrifice his life
rationale: Such a man commands our approbation.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: the scholar trained for public duty

recommendation: When gain is offered, think of righteousness.
evidence_quote:
When
the opportunity of gain is presented to him, he thinks of
righteousness.
rationale: Such a man commands our approbation.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: the scholar trained for public duty

recommendation: Be reverential in sacrificing, and in mourning think of the grief you should feel.
evidence_quote:
In sacrificing, his thoughts are reverential. In
mourning, his thoughts are about the grief which he should feel.
rationale: Such a man commands our approbation.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
scope: the scholar trained for public duty

recommendation: Seek to enlarge the virtue you hold and believe right principles with firm sincerity.
evidence_quote:
holds fast to virtue,
but without seeking to enlarge it, and believes right principles, but
without firm sincerity
rationale: A man who lacks these is of no account, whether he exists or not.
argued_against: Holding virtue without enlarging it; belief without sincerity

recommendation: Honor the talented and virtuous, bear with all, praise the good, and pity the incompetent.
evidence_quote:
The superior
man honours the talented and virtuous, and bears with all. He
praises the good, and pities the incompetent.
rationale: If you are talented you can bear with anyone; if not, men will put you away; there is no reason to put others away.
argued_against: Associating only with those who can advantage you and dropping those who cannot

recommendation: Do not practice minor studies that become inapplicable when carried to what is remote.
evidence_quote:
there is a danger of
their proving inapplicable. Therefore, the superior man does not
practise them.
rationale: Inferior studies have something worth looking at but risk being inapplicable when pushed far.
conditions: Applies when carried to what is remote
argued_against: Pursuing inferior studies to remote ends

recommendation: Each day recognize what you do not yet know, and each month do not forget what you have attained.
evidence_quote:
He, who from day to day recognises
what he has not yet, and from month to month does not forget what
he has attained to, may be said indeed to love to learn.
rationale: This is what it means to love to learn.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Learn extensively, hold a firm and sincere aim, inquire earnestly, and reflect with self-application.
evidence_quote:
learning extensively, and
having a firm and sincere aim; inquiring with earnestness, and
reflecting with self-application
rationale: Virtue is in such a course.

recommendation: Learn in order to reach the utmost of your principles.
evidence_quote:
The superior man
learns, in order to reach to the utmost of his principles.
rationale: A mechanic has a shop to accomplish his works; the superior man learns to reach the utmost of his principles.

recommendation: Do not gloss over your faults.
evidence_quote:
The mean man is sure to gloss his
faults.
rationale: none given
argued_against: The mean man who glosses faults

recommendation: When you have faults, change them openly; people will look up to you.
evidence_quote: he changes again, and all men look up to him
rationale: A superior man's faults are seen by all like eclipses, but his change earns respect.

recommendation: Win the people's confidence before imposing labors on them.
evidence_quote:
The superior man, having obtained
their confidence, may then impose labours on his people.
rationale: Without their confidence, the people will think he is oppressing them.
conditions: Only after obtaining the people's confidence

recommendation: Win your prince's confidence before you remonstrate with him.
evidence_quote:
Having obtained the confidence of his prince, one may then
remonstrate with him.
rationale: Without his confidence the prince will think you are vilifying him.
conditions: Only after gaining the prince's confidence

recommendation: Do not transgress the boundary in great virtues; some latitude is allowed in small virtues.
evidence_quote:
When a person does not transgress
the boundary line in the great virtues, he may pass and repass it in
the small virtues.
rationale: none given
conditions: Latitude applies only if great virtues are kept

recommendation: An officer should devote leisure to learning; a student who has finished learning should become an officer.
evidence_quote:
The officer, having discharged all
his duties, should devote his leisure to learning. The student, having
completed his learning, should apply himself to be an officer.
rationale: none given
conditions: After discharging duties or completing learning

recommendation: In mourning, stop once grief has reached its utmost.
evidence_quote:
Mourning, having been carried to
the utmost degree of grief, should stop with that.
rationale: none given

recommendation: When judging an accusation, be grieved and pity the accused; do not feel joy at your own ability.
evidence_quote:
be
grieved for and pity them, and do not feel joy at your own ability
rationale: Rulers have failed in their duties and the people have long been disorganised.
conditions: When you have found out the truth of an accusation
argued_against: Pride in one's skill as a judge

recommendation: Avoid placing yourself in a low position where all the evil of the world flows in on you.
evidence_quote:
the superior man hates to dwell

in a low-lying situation, where all the evil of the world will flow in
upon him
rationale: Even a wicked man is blamed for more than he did; once low, all evil is attributed to him.
argued_against: Dwelling in a low, disreputable position

recommendation: Honor your father by not changing his ministers or his mode of government.
evidence_quote:
not changing the ministers of his father, nor his father's mode of
government, it is difficult to be attained to
rationale: This filial conduct is harder to attain than ordinary filial acts.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Seek true knowledge: see one changeless life in all lives.
evidence_quote: To see one changeless Life in all the Lives
rationale: Knowledge of this kind is true, unlike seeing separate existences as real or clinging blindly to one thing as all.
argued_against: Seeing separate existences as real; narrow, dark clinging to one thing

recommendation: Act without attachment and passionlessly, for duty, not for love, hate, or gain.
evidence_quote:
Is wrought without attachment, passionlessly,
  For duty, not for love, nor hate, nor gain.
rationale: This is right action, unlike action driven by desire and self (Rajas) or heedless action (Tamas).
argued_against: Action driven by desire and egoism

recommendation: Do not act heedless of consequences, of harm to others, or of harm to your own soul.
evidence_quote:
heedless of the hurt
  Or wrong for others
rationale: Such action is of Tamas, black and bad.

recommendation: Act free from self-seeking, humble, resolute, steadfast, the same in good or evil fortune, content to do right.
evidence_quote:
Free from self-seeking, humble, resolute,
  Steadfast, in good or evil hap the same
rationale: Such a doer truly acts, unlike the impassioned and the dark doer.
argued_against: Impassioned doers who seek profit; loose-hearted, stubborn, fraudulent doers

recommendation: Cultivate an intellect that knows what must and must not be done, what to fear, and what binds or frees the soul.
evidence_quote: What must be done, and what must not be done
rationale: This is the good (Sattwic) intellect, unlike the intellect that knows right but lacks firmness or that mistakes wrong for right.
argued_against: Intellect that sees wrong as right

recommendation: Master your heart, breath, and senses, fixed in unshaken faith and piety.
evidence_quote:
Masters his beats of heart, his very breath
  Of life, the action of his senses
rationale: This is good steadfastness, unlike holding to duty for gain or clinging to sloth, sorrow, and fear.
argued_against: Steadfastness in sloth, fear, and despair

recommendation: Seek the lasting pleasure born of inner contentment, bitter at first and sweet later; avoid pleasure from senses, sloth, and sin.
evidence_quote: Sweet as the taste of Amrit. Drink of that!
rationale: Sense pleasure tastes sweet first and bitter last; pleasure from sloth and sin bewilders the soul throughout.
argued_against: Pleasure from sense contact, sloth, sin, and foolishness

recommendation: Perform diligently and contentedly the work allotted to you, whatever it is.
evidence_quote:
Whoso performeth--diligent, content--
  The work allotted him, whate'er it be,
  Lays hold of perfectness!
rationale: Perfection is found through worship of the Source of all, wrought by work.
scope: each person by nature and class (Brahman, Kshatriya, Vaisya, Sudra)

recommendation: Do your own work, though flawed, rather than another's work done excellently.
evidence_quote:
Better thine own work is, though done with fault,
  Than doing others' work, ev'n excellently.
rationale: He who faces the task set by nature does not fall into sin.

recommendation: Never abandon your natural duty, though it bears blame.
evidence_quote:
Let no man leave
  His natural duty, Prince! though it bear blame!
rationale: Every work has blame as every flame has smoke; only one who works with unfettered mind and renounced results attains release from work.
argued_against: Abandoning duty because it brings blame

recommendation: Practice self-control, spare diet, solitude, and constant holy meditation, free of passions, pride, and anger.
evidence_quote: Ever to holy meditation vowed
rationale: Such a person becomes one with Brahm, serene, sorrowless, loving all beings, and attains the Supreme.

recommendation: Do all you do for the Lord, renounce for Him, sacrifice heart, mind, and will to Him, and live in faith in Him.
evidence_quote:
Do all thou dost for Me! Renounce for Me!
  Sacrifice heart and mind and will to Me!
  Live in the faith of Me!
rationale: By His grace all dangers are vanquished; trusting oneself and heeding not leads to perishing.

recommendation: Do not refuse to fight out of self-reliance; your own nature will drive you to the task.
evidence_quote:
Relying on thyself, "I will not fight!"
  Vain will the purpose prove!
rationale: Your qualities would spur you to war; what you shun through illusion you would seek against your will.
argued_against: Relying on oneself; refusing duty out of illusion

recommendation: Trust the Master in the heart wholly and take Him as your support.
evidence_quote:
With all thy soul
  Trust Him, and take Him for thy succour, Prince!
rationale: Only so will you gain, by His grace, the uttermost repose and the Eternal Place.

recommendation: Meditate on this teaching, then act as you choose.
evidence_quote: Meditate!
rationale: This is the Truth of Truths, more hidden than any secret.

recommendation: Give your heart to the Lord, adore Him, serve Him, and cling to Him in faith, love, and reverence.
evidence_quote:
Give Me thy heart! adore Me! serve Me! cling
  In faith and love and reverence to Me!
rationale: Thereby you will come to Him; the promise is true and the addressee is dear to Him.

recommendation: Let go of rites and written duties and make the Lord your single refuge.
evidence_quote:
Rites and writ duties! Fly to Me alone!
  Make Me thy single refuge!
rationale: He will free the soul from all its sins; be of good cheer.
argued_against: Reliance on rites and written duties

recommendation: Do not share this teaching with those who lack faith, do not worship, or mock.
evidence_quote: Hide it from all men who mock
rationale: none given

recommendation: Teach this supreme teaching among the Lord's devotees, in faith.
evidence_quote:
wherever, 'mid the flock
  Of My lovers, one shall teach
  This  divinest, wisest, speech
rationale: No deed is dearer to Him; the teacher comes to Brahma.

recommendation: Read and ponder this dialogue piously, or hear it with faith and meekness.
evidence_quote:
Whoso reads this converse o'er,
  Held by Us upon the plain,
  Pondering piously and fain,
  He hath paid Me sacrifice!
rationale: Reading counts as sacrifice; one who hears it wisely and meekly rises at death to the realms of the Blest.

recommendation: Do not depend on one resource; keep everything double, especially the causes of success, favor, and esteem.
evidence_quote:
Everything 
should  be  kept  double,  especially  the  causes  of 
success,  of  favour,  or  of  esteem.
rationale: It doubles your life; things dependent on human will are brittle; Nature gives duplicate vital limbs, so Art should duplicate qualities we depend on.
scope: all people, the sage in particular
argued_against: Trusting to one resource however pre-eminent

recommendation: Do not nourish the spirit of contradiction.
evidence_quote: Do  not  nourish  the  Spirit  of  Contradiction.
rationale: It proves you foolish or peevish and turns pleasant conversation into mimic war against associates.

recommendation: Post yourself in the center of things.
evidence_quote: Post  Yourself  in  the  Centre  of  Things.
rationale: You feel the pulse of affairs; many lose their way in useless discussion and waste time on side matters.
argued_against: Verbosity and fussing over a single point

recommendation: Be self-sufficient: be your own universal friend and able to live alone.
evidence_quote:
let  a  man  be  his  own  universal 
friend,  and  then  he  is  in  a  position  to  live  alone.
rationale: Depending on oneself alone is the highest happiness and like the Supreme Being; one who can live alone resembles the sage and God.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: In storms of public or private life, hold your hand and let things calm down of themselves.
evidence_quote:
The  proper  way  to  still 
the  storms  of  the  vulgar  is  to  hold  your  hand 
and  let  them  calm  down  of  themselves.
rationale: Remedies often make diseases worse; a fountain clears by being left alone; giving way now conquers later.
conditions: Applies more the wilder the waves of life
argued_against: Meddling and applying remedies at wrong times

recommendation: Recognize unlucky days; two tries are enough to tell whether you are in luck today.
evidence_quote:
Two  tries  should  be  enough  to 
tell  if  one  is  in  luck  to-day  or  not.
rationale: Everything changes, even the mind; things must be done on their own day.

recommendation: On lucky days, seize the occasion and do not throw away the slightest chance.
evidence_quote:
At  such 
times  one  must  seize  the  occasion  and  not 
throw  away  the  slightest  chance.
rationale: On lucky days everything is ready, wit prompt, and the genius favorable.
conditions: Applies when one is in luck

recommendation: Do not judge the day's luck by a single piece of good or bad fortune.
evidence_quote:
a 
shrewd  person   will    not  decide   on    the  day's

luck  by  a  single  piece  of  good  or  bad  fortune
rationale: One may be only a lucky chance and the other only a slight annoyance.

recommendation: Find the good in a thing at once.
evidence_quote: Find  the  Good  in  a  Thing  at  once,
rationale: Nothing lacks good; those who fix on one defect among a thousand excellences lead a sad life, feeding on bitters.
argued_against: Fault-finding as scavengers of men's minds

recommendation: Do not listen to yourself when speaking.
evidence_quote:
To  speak  and  at  the  same  time  listen 
to  yourself  cannot  turn  out  well.
rationale: Pleasing yourself without pleasing others brings general contempt; the pompous seek applause at every sentence.
argued_against: The pompous who need a stupid bravo at every word

recommendation: Never take the wrong side out of obstinacy because your opponent has already taken the right one.
evidence_quote:
it  would  be  folly  to  come  lagging  after 
with  the  worst
rationale: You begin beaten and cannot win with bad weapons; the obstinate lose the true by contradicting it; taking the better course yourself drives a foolish opponent off it.
argued_against: Obstinacy; siding with passion against right

recommendation: Never become paradoxical in order to avoid the trite.
evidence_quote:
Never  become  Paradoxical  in  order  to 
avoid  the  Trite.
rationale: Both extremes damage reputation; paradox wins applause at first but is discredited when its emptiness appears, and it shows unbalanced judgment.
argued_against: Paradox as a cheat to avoid the direct road of excellence

recommendation: Begin with another's aim to end with your own; never advance except under cover.
evidence_quote: Begin  with  Another's  to  end  with  your  Own.
rationale: Foreseen advantages lure the other's will; it also helps with those who always say no first; ground is dangerous.
conditions: One should never advance unless under cover, especially where the ground is dangerous

recommendation: Regularly examine your ruling faculty: its nature, its purpose, and whether it is understanding, social, and free of the flesh.
evidence_quote:
What is my ruling faculty now to me? and of what nature am I now
making it?
rationale: none given
argued_against: A ruling faculty void of understanding, cut off from social life, or melted into the flesh

recommendation: Do not be grieved, angry, or afraid about what the ruling Law assigns; doing so is running away from your master.
evidence_quote:
He then who fears or
is grieved or is angry is a runaway.
rationale: The law is master and assigns to everyone what is fit; one who is dissatisfied with what is appointed flees his master.

recommendation: Constantly consider that all things now were the same in time past and will be the same again.
evidence_quote:
Constantly consider how all things such as they now are, in time
past also were; and consider that they will be the same again.
rationale: Past courts and dramas of history were the same as now, only with different actors.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition

recommendation: Do not grieve or be discontented at what happens; follow it voluntarily.
evidence_quote:
Imagine every man who is grieved at anything or discontented to be
like a pig which is sacrificed and kicks and screams.
rationale: Only the rational animal can follow voluntarily what happens; following is a necessity for all.
argued_against: Lamenting one's bonds; kicking and screaming like a pig

recommendation: On every action, pause and ask whether death is dreadful because it deprives you of this.
evidence_quote:
Severally on the occasion of everything that thou dost, pause and
ask thyself if death is a dreadful thing because it deprives thee of
this.
rationale: none given

recommendation: When offended at someone's fault, turn to yourself and reflect on how you err in a like manner.
evidence_quote:
When thou art offended at any man's fault, forthwith turn to thyself
and reflect in what like manner thou dost err thyself
rationale: You will quickly forget your anger, especially if you consider that the man is compelled and could not do otherwise.
argued_against: Anger at others' faults; thinking money, pleasure, or reputation are goods

recommendation: If you are able, remove the compulsion acting on the person who offends you.
evidence_quote:
or, if thou art able, take away
from him the compulsion
rationale: The offender acts under compulsion.

recommendation: Be content to pass your short life in an orderly way, seeing human things as smoke.
evidence_quote:
And why art thou
not content to pass through this short time in an orderly way?
rationale: Famous men are nowhere now and what has changed never returns; events are exercises for the reason.
argued_against: Avoiding the matter and opportunity for activity

recommendation: Persevere until you have made these examinations of life your own.
evidence_quote:
Persevere then until thou shalt have made these things
thy own
rationale: As a strengthened stomach digests everything and a blazing fire turns all into flame.

recommendation: Be simple and good, so that no one can truly say otherwise.
evidence_quote:
Let it not be in any man's power to say truly of thee that thou are
not simple or that thou art not good
rationale: It is entirely in your power; nothing hinders you, and reason does not allow you to live if you are not such.

recommendation: Do and say what is most conformable to reason, and make no excuses that you are hindered.
evidence_quote:
it
is in thy power to do it or to say it, and do not make excuses that thou
art hindered.
rationale: Reason passes through all obstacles; other obstacles affect only the body or harm only through opinion and the reason's own yielding.
argued_against: Making excuses that one is hindered

recommendation: Treat as an enjoyment everything within your power that accords with your own nature.
evidence_quote:
a
man ought to consider as an enjoyment everything which it is in his
power to do according to his own nature
rationale: It is in his power everywhere, unlike things governed by nature or an irrational soul.

recommendation: Make right use of misfortunes, so that you become better and more worthy of praise.
evidence_quote:
more worthy of praise by making a right
use of these accidents
